# A2UI

> A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open-source generative UI framework and streaming protocol. Agents compose declarative surfaces, registered catalog components, and reactive data models (via A2UI Express, Jev-style decision models, or server-side macros), while clients render them with native framework widgets across React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. No untrusted code is executed on the client. Protocol versions: v1.0 (current), v0.9.1 (previous), v0.9 (previous), v0.8 (deprecated).

Parallel Markdown editions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to the route path (for example, `https://a2ui.org/quickstart.md` or `https://a2ui.org/concepts/overview.md`), and the combined documentation corpus is served at [llms-full.txt](https://a2ui.org/llms-full.txt).

## Agent Harness Skills & Visual Tools

- Agent skills CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf): `npx skills add a2ui-project/a2ui`
- [Get Help & Agent Skills](https://a2ui.org/get-help/)
- [Build with A2UI: generative UI spectrum and production stories](https://a2ui.org/build-with-a2ui/)
- [A2UI Composer & Inspector](https://a2ui-editor.ag-ui.com)
- [A2UI Playground](https://go.copilotkit.ai/a2ui-playground)

## When to Use A2UI

- Dynamic multi-step user journeys where static tool-bound cards are too rigid, while arbitrary iframe code would break native brand consistency, accessibility, or security boundaries.
- Cross-platform generative UI rendered natively on Web (React, Lit, Angular), mobile/desktop (Flutter, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Lynx), or terminal (Go Bubble Tea, Ink) from a single agent stream.
- Remote, multi-agent, or cross-trust-boundary integrations where agents must send declarative data rather than executable code.
- Flutter projects: use [`a2ui_flutter`](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_flutter) with [`a2ui_core`](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_core) (and [`a2ui_agent`](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_agent) when calling models from Dart). Do not use the discontinued `flutter_genui` or `genui_a2ui` packages.

## Install Official SDKs

- React: `npm install @a2ui/react @a2ui/web_core`
- Lit: `npm install @a2ui/lit @a2ui/web_core`
- Angular: `npm install @a2ui/angular @a2ui/web_core`
- Flutter: `flutter pub add a2ui_flutter a2ui_core`
- Swift (SPM): `https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui` (`A2UISwiftCore`, `A2UISwiftUI`, `BasicCatalogSwiftUI`)
- Android Jetpack Compose (Google Maven): `androidx.compose.material3:material3-a2ui`, `androidx.a2ui.compose:compose-ui`, `androidx.a2ui.compose:compose-runtime`, and `androidx.a2ui:a2ui-model`
- Agent SDKs: `pip install a2ui-agent-sdk` (Python, plus `a2ui-adk` and `a2ui-a2a`); `npm install @a2ui/agent` (TypeScript); `dart pub add a2ui_agent` (Dart)

# Quickstart

> Run a small A2UI app, a Python agent server with a React web client and a Flutter mobile client, from one prompt to your coding agent or in three commands.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/quickstart/

**A2UI** lets an AI agent answer with an interface instead of a paragraph:
cards your users can tap, dates they can drag, a panel that keeps up with them.

This quickstart runs **Travel A2UI**, a small trip planner built on the official
A2UI SDKs. It is simple on purpose: **one Python server** holds the agent, and
a **React** client (web) and a **Flutter** client (mobile) draw what it sends.
Paste one of these prompts into your coding agent:
- **Web + Mobile (Python + React + Flutter):** `Follow the steps at https://a2ui.org/quickstart/agent.md to set up the A2UI quickstart web and mobile apps and explain them to me.`
- **Web only (Python + React):** `Follow the steps at https://a2ui.org/quickstart/agent/web.md to set up the A2UI quickstart web app and explain it to me.`
- **Mobile only (Python + Flutter):** `Follow the steps at https://a2ui.org/quickstart/agent/mobile.md to set up the A2UI quickstart mobile app and explain it to me.`

Or follow the [step-by-step walkthrough](/quickstart/step-by-step/).
> **Note**
  Travel A2UI lives in A2UI Labs, at
  [samples/travel-a2ui](https://github.com/a2ui-project/labs/tree/main/samples/travel-a2ui). It is a
  sample for learning A2UI and is not meant for production use.

## How A2UI fits into this app

A2UI is an SDK for your agent and a renderer for your app. Here is where each
part lives in Travel A2UI:

One server serves the API, the React app at `/` and the Flutter app at
`/flutter/`. The clients know nothing about travel: each knows how to draw the
catalog's components. You, the builder, decide what is in the catalog; the
agent decides what to draw from it. [How A2UI works](/concepts/overview/)
walks through the same picture for any A2UI app.

## What you will learn

Once it runs, your agent (or the [step-by-step walkthrough](/quickstart/step-by-step/))
explains, with the app open:

1. **What on screen is A2UI** and what is ordinary app code: surfaces, the
   components in them, and the data they show.
2. **The catalog**: the components and client functions the agent may use,
   and why it is the guardrail.
3. **Agent skills**: how the model is taught to write A2UI for the catalog.
4. **What the model writes versus what the client receives**: A2UI Express,
   the A2UI messages the agent SDK turns it into, and the MessageProcessor
   that applies them.
5. **Renderers**: the two here, and the others A2UI has.

## Other fast paths

To try A2UI without cloning anything:

- **Agent skills**: run `npx skills add a2ui-project/a2ui` in your project to give your coding agent A2UI's protocol rules, SDK integration guides and catalog authoring workflows (see [Get Help](/get-help/)).
- **[A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-editor.ag-ui.com)** ([source](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/tools/composer)): a visual workspace for prompting an assistant, inspecting streamed messages and `dataModel` updates, and editing surfaces side by side.
- **[A2UI Playground](https://go.copilotkit.ai/a2ui-playground)**: a browser sandbox for trying A2UI prompts and component catalogs with no local setup.

---

# Step-by-Step Walkthrough

> Run Travel A2UI yourself, with a React web client, a Flutter mobile client or both, then learn how A2UI works from what is on screen, with screenshots and real output.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/quickstart/step-by-step/

Run the app first, then read the second half with it open: every idea there is
something you can see on screen. The app is [samples/travel-a2ui](https://github.com/a2ui-project/labs/tree/main/samples/travel-a2ui)
in A2UI Labs: one Python server, a React client for the web and a Flutter client
for mobile.

## Run it

You need **Python 3.11+**, plus **Node 20+** for the web app and
**Flutter 3.38+** for the mobile app.

1. Get the code:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/a2ui-project/labs
   cd labs/samples/travel-a2ui
   ```

2. Start the server with both clients:

   ```bash
   ./scripts/quickstart.sh both
   ```

   Or `react` for the web app only, or `flutter` for the mobile app only. The
   script installs the server into `.venv`, builds the clients (Flutter takes
   about a minute) and starts the server. Its output, trimmed (your versions
   will differ):

   ```text
   → Checking what is installed
     Python 3.11.18
     node v22.23.4
   → The Python server
     installed into .venv
   → The React client
   ✓ built in 456ms
   → The Flutter client
   ✓ Built build/web
   → Starting on port 8080
     React:   http://127.0.0.1:8080
     Flutter: http://127.0.0.1:8080/flutter/
     No GEMINI_API_KEY set: paste a key into the app when it asks.
   ```

3. Open the web app at [http://127.0.0.1:8080](http://127.0.0.1:8080) and the
   mobile app at [http://127.0.0.1:8080/flutter/](http://127.0.0.1:8080/flutter/).

### The web app

![The React client: flight cards in the conversation, the trip so far beside it](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases/download/docs-assets/quickstart--travel-a2ui--chat.a481b6c8.webp)

You land on a recorded sample trip, no key needed. To talk to the agent, paste
a free Gemini key from [AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) when the
app asks (it stays in your browser), then try _"Six days in Madrid in April,
two of us, around $2,500 all in"_.

### The mobile app

<img
  src="https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases/download/docs-assets/quickstart--travel-a2ui--flutter-trip.8afa2402.webp"
  width="224"
  height="485"
  loading="lazy"
  decoding="async"
  alt="The Flutter client in a phone layout, with the trip sheet open"
  style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 14rem; height: auto; margin-inline: auto;"
/>

Paste your key, then try _"A weekend in Lisbon from JFK in May, two of us"_.
Here Flutter is built for the web, in a phone layout; the same Dart code can
target iOS and Android, which this sample does not set up. Ask both apps the
same thing: the same messages, drawn by two renderers.

## How A2UI works

Five short steps, in the order you meet them on screen: what on the screen is
A2UI, what the agent is allowed to draw, how the model learns it, what travels
to the client, and what draws it. For all of it in one picture, see
[how A2UI fits into this app](/quickstart/#how-a2ui-fits-into-this-app).

### 1. What is A2UI, and what is app code

Not everything on screen is A2UI. Blue is composed by the agent; grey is app
code, written by you, the builder, and the same on every turn:

![The app with A2UI surfaces outlined in blue (a cost card in the conversation and the trip panel) and app code outlined in grey (the header, the message box and the reply text)](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases/download/docs-assets/quickstart--travel-a2ui--a2ui-vs-app.6cf941df.webp)

- **A2UI, composed by the agent:** the cards in the conversation, the trip
  panel (the trip sheet in Flutter) and the web client's Home dashboard.
- **App code:** the header and tabs, the message box, the chat bubbles (the
  model's words, shown as plain text), the key form, and the Catalog and Wire
  tabs.

Each blue region is a **surface**: one area of UI the agent controls. A surface
is made of **components** (a `Text`, a `Button`, a `FlightOption`), and the
values they show come from the surface's **data model**. When the user taps a
flight, the agent receives an **action** saying which one.

A rule of thumb for your own app: if it should look the same on every turn,
build it yourself as app code; if it depends on what the user just asked, let
the agent compose it.

### 2. The catalog: what the agent may draw

The **catalog** (`catalogs/a2ui-travel/catalog.json`) lists everything the
agent may use, and it holds two kinds of thing:

- **Components**, and the properties each takes. A2UI's **basic catalog**
  provides `Text`, `Row`, `Column`, `List`, `Button`, `TextField` and more;
  this app adds travel components such as `FlightOption`, `HotelCard`,
  `DateRangePicker` and `PriceSummary`. A component can hold others, so a card
  is a small arrangement of catalog components.
- **Functions**, which run in the client. The basic ones format and check
  values (`formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `pluralize`, `required`); this app
  adds `calcNights` and `equals`. A component can show a function's result, so
  the night count follows the dates the user picks, with no turn to the agent:

  ```text
  "${calcNights(start: ${/trip/startDate}, end: ${/trip/endDate})} nights"
  ```

The web client's **Catalog** tab draws every component with the real renderer:

![The Catalog tab: every component the agent may use, drawn by the real renderer](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases/download/docs-assets/quickstart--travel-a2ui--catalog.f3f5e3ff.webp)

The catalog is also the **guardrail**. The server checks every message the
model writes against it before sending anything, and each client implements
every component and function in it, so the agent can only ask for what the
client knows how to draw. The work splits between the model and you, the
builder:

| The model decides                | You, the builder, decide                           |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Whether to show a card           | Which components and functions exist (the catalog) |
| Which components, and the layout | The data in them                                   |
| The wording                      | That every message is checked against the catalog  |
| What to ask next                 | What a press records                               |

### 3. Skills: teaching the model A2UI

A **skill** is a Markdown file that teaches a model to write A2UI for a
catalog. This app has two, in `skills/express-modular/`: `a2ui-core` teaches
the notation, and `a2ui-travel` teaches this catalog. Here is an entry from the
second:

```text
• FlightOption(airline, departTime,
    arriveTime, origin, destination,
    price, action (static), duration?,
    stops?, flightNumber?, …)
  - Description: A single selectable
    flight itinerary leg. Use one per
    option when presenting a choice
    of flights.
  - airline: Operating carrier,
    e.g. 'Iberia' or 'Delta'.
```

Here the skills are generated from the catalog with the A2UI agent SDK's
`SkillGenerator` (`scripts/build_skills.py`), so when a component changes,
`npm run generate` updates what the model is taught to match.

### 4. What the model writes, and what the client receives

The model writes **A2UI Express**, a short notation, as its skills taught it.
`root` comes first, so the card can appear before the rest is written:

```text
root = Column([head, list])
head = Text("### Flights to Madrid")
list = List(_template($/flights, fare))
fare = FlightOption($airline,
  $departTime, $arriveTime,
  $origin, $destination, $price,
  Event("select_flight", {id: $id}))
```

On the server, the **A2UI agent SDK** reads the Express as the model streams
it, turns it into **A2UI messages** and checks each against the catalog. The
messages are JSON: `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel` and
`deleteSurface`. Here is the component list one of these blocks became (trimmed
to ids and links): each component names its children by id, starting from
`root`.

```json
[
  {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["head", "list"]},
  {"id": "head", "component": "Text", "text": "### Flights to Madrid"},
  {"id": "fare", "component": "FlightOption"},
  {
    "id": "list",
    "component": "List",
    "children": {"path": "/flights", "componentId": "fare"}
  }
]
```

In the client, a **MessageProcessor** from the A2UI SDK applies the messages:
it keeps each surface's components and data, fills in bound values, runs
catalog functions, and sends presses back as actions. React uses
`@a2ui/web_core`'s (`apps/web/src/surfaces.ts`); Flutter uses `a2ui_core`'s
(`apps/flutter/lib/chat.dart`).

The web client's **Wire** tab shows both forms of every surface side by side,
what the model wrote and what the client received:

![The Wire tab: the Express the model wrote, beside the A2UI JSON the client received](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/releases/download/docs-assets/quickstart--travel-a2ui--wire.4515c08f.webp)

Express is one way for a model to write A2UI, chosen because it is short. A2UI
itself is the JSON.

### 5. Renderers

A **renderer** implements the catalog's components with native widgets and
uses a MessageProcessor to apply messages. It holds no app logic.

- **In this app:** React (`@a2ui/react`, `@a2ui/web_core`) in
  `renderers/react/`, and Flutter (`a2ui_flutter`, `a2ui_core`) in
  `renderers/flutter/`. The apps around them are `apps/web/` and
  `apps/flutter/`.
- **[Maintained by the A2UI project](/concepts/sdks/#renderer-sdk):** Lit
  (web components), Angular, React, Flutter, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose and
  Markdown.
- **[From the community](/ecosystem/renderers/):** UIKit, React Native,
  Vue, Lynx, a terminal renderer and more.

The server never knows which client it is talking to. Adding a platform means
writing a renderer for the same catalog, with no change to the agent.

## Deploy to Cloud Run

Run the quickstart app in your own Google Cloud project: the server and both
clients on one URL. You need a project with billing enabled.

[![Open in Cloud Shell](https://gstatic.com/cloudssh/images/open-btn.svg)](https://shell.cloud.google.com/cloudshell/editor?cloudshell_git_repo=https://github.com/a2ui-project/labs&cloudshell_git_branch=main&cloudshell_workspace=samples/travel-a2ui&cloudshell_tutorial=docs/cloud-shell.md&show=ide%2Cterminal)

Cloud Shell opens with the sample and a short guide beside the terminal: sign
in, choose a project, and run one script:

```bash
./scripts/deploy.sh
```

It turns on the services the deploy needs, lets the build use them, then builds
and deploys (about ten minutes the first time) and prints the URL. No key is
stored on the service: each visitor pastes their own. From your own clone, the
same script works anywhere the gcloud CLI is signed in; see
[deploying](https://github.com/a2ui-project/labs/blob/main/samples/travel-a2ui/docs/deploying.md)
for what it runs.

  this app about something other than travel.

# Overview: How A2UI Works

> How the A2UI agent SDK, transport, and client renderer fit together, traced through a single request.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/overview/

A2UI lets an AI agent describe an interactive UI as a stream of JSON messages that a client app renders with its own native widgets. Below you'll find the mechanics on each side of the connection, how they fit together, and one request traced from the user's prompt to a button tap.

---

## Generating UI

On the server, you configure the [A2UI Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) with a [component catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) (`catalog.json`) that describes the UI components and functions available to render on your client. From that catalog, the SDK's skill generator produces an A2UI skill containing prompt instructions and grammar rules. Your agent code and LLM runtime sit outside the SDK: they take the generated A2UI skill alongside your domain tools (such as a flight search API), call the model, and pass its UI output to the SDK's compiler. The compiler parses and validates the content against the catalog, then sends layout ([`updateComponents`](/concepts/messages/)) and data ([`updateDataModel`](/concepts/messages/)) messages over a transport such as AG-UI, A2A, MCP, or WebSockets.

On the client, your app hosts an [A2UI Renderer](/concepts/sdks/#renderer-sdk), which draws the UI with native platform widgets inside a region of your screen called a surface. Controls bound to the surface's [data model](/concepts/data-binding/) update state locally as the user interacts with them, and user triggers such as button taps send [`action`](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) messages back to the agent.

While this page focuses on generating UI at request time, A2UI content can also be authored in advance and sent as a static payload (for example, returned from an MCP server via an agent to a client), following a traditional server-driven UI pattern.

_In the diagram above, purple marks your server-side agent code, blue marks your client app, and the teal dashed outlines mark the A2UI libraries on each side (the Agent SDK on the server and the Renderer on the client)._

---

## Step-by-step generation

The rest of this page traces a flight-booking request through each stage of the pipeline: defining the catalog, generating the skill, prompting the model, compiling and validating the output, rendering the surface on the client, and handling user actions.

### Define the catalog

You define the components and functions your client can render in `catalog.json`. A travel app might pair the basic catalog with domain components such as `FlightCard`. Each component declares its properties with JSON Schema, so the Agent SDK can validate that the model only emits components and properties the client knows how to draw:

#### v1.0

{/* prettier-ignore */}
```jsonc
{
  "protocolVersion": "1.0",
  "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json",
  "components": {
    "FlightCard": {
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Displays a flight segment with fare and passenger count.",
      "properties": {
        "component": {"const": "FlightCard"},
        "flightNumber": {
          "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
          "description": "IATA flight designator, such as 'LH 454'."
        }
        // ... origin, destination, price, passengers
      },
      "required": ["component", "flightNumber", "origin", "destination", "price", "passengers"]
    }
    // ... other components and functions
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

{/* prettier-ignore */}
```jsonc
{
  "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v0_9/catalog.json",
  "components": {
    "FlightCard": {
      "type": "object",
      "allOf": [
        {"$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/ComponentCommon"},
        {
          "type": "object",
          "description": "Displays a flight segment with fare and passenger count.",
          "properties": {
            "component": {"const": "FlightCard"},
            "flightNumber": {
              "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
              "description": "IATA flight designator, such as 'LH 454'."
            }
            // ... origin, destination, price, passengers
          },
          "required": ["component", "flightNumber", "origin", "destination", "price", "passengers"]
        }
      ],
      "unevaluatedProperties": false
    }
    // ... other components and functions
  }
}
```

### Generate the skill

From `catalog.json`, the Agent SDK's skill generator builds an A2UI skill containing grammar rules for the chosen [inference format](/concepts/inference-formats/) (such as Express) together with component and function signatures derived directly from your catalog:

```text
---
name: a2ui
description: Generates interactive user interface components for user requests.
---

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: You MUST always surround the entire A2UI Express block with the literal sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`...

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   ...
   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.
...
6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
...

## Positional Component Signatures
...
• FlightCard(flightNumber, origin, destination, price, passengers)
  - Description: Displays a flight segment with fare and passenger count.
  - flightNumber: IATA flight designator, such as 'LH 454'.
  ...
```

### Prompt the model

The user types a request in the client app:

> _"Berlin to San Francisco today, and two tickets back on Oct 19."_

Your agent then:

1. Calls its domain tools, for example `searchFlights(from: "BER", to: "SFO", date: "2026-10-12")`, to get flights and prices.
2. Decides that a form with passenger counts is more useful here than a paragraph of text.
3. Loads the generated A2UI skill and prompts the model with the flight data.

### Compile and validate the output

The model streams its answer. Instead of writing wire JSON directly, it can use a compact inference format such as Express:

```text
<a2ui>
$/outbound/pax = 1
$/outbound/price = 455
$/return/pax = 2
$/return/price = 970

root = Card(Column([
  FlightCard(flightNumber="LH 454", origin="BER", destination="SFO", price=$/outbound/price, passengers=$/outbound/pax),
  FlightCard(flightNumber="UA 901", origin="SFO", destination="BER", price=$/return/price, passengers=$/return/pax),
  Button(Text("Confirm booking"), variant="primary", action=Event("confirm_booking", {outboundPax: $/outbound/pax, returnPax: $/return/pax}))
]))
</a2ui>
```

The Agent SDK compiler processes the stream as it arrives:

1. Parses incoming tokens into an intermediate representation.
2. Validates that each component exists in the catalog and that its properties match the schema, reporting invalid output as soon as it appears.
3. Emits the wire messages: `createSurface` opens the surface on the client, `updateComponents` sends the validated component list, and `updateDataModel` sends the initial data values.

#### Messages on the wire

The tabs below show the `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, and `updateDataModel` messages for this example. Component IDs are chosen by the compiler; the ones here are for readability.

#### v1.0

Surface creation message, defined by [`CreateSurfaceMessage`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage) (shown separately from `updateComponents` and `updateDataModel` below to illustrate each message type; in v1.0, the compiler can also inline initial `components` and `dataModel` inside `createSurface`):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json"
  }
}
```

Layout message, defined by [`UpdateComponentsMessage`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateComponents": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "components": [
      {"id": "root", "component": "Card", "child": "layout_col"},
      {
        "id": "layout_col",
        "component": "Column",
        "children": ["flight_outbound", "flight_return", "submit_btn"]
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_outbound",
        "component": "FlightCard",
        "flightNumber": "LH 454",
        "origin": "BER",
        "destination": "SFO",
        "price": {"@path": "/outbound/price"},
        "passengers": {"@path": "/outbound/pax"}
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_return",
        "component": "FlightCard",
        "flightNumber": "UA 901",
        "origin": "SFO",
        "destination": "BER",
        "price": {"@path": "/return/price"},
        "passengers": {"@path": "/return/pax"}
      },
      {"id": "submit_label", "component": "Text", "text": "Confirm booking"},
      {
        "id": "submit_btn",
        "component": "Button",
        "child": "submit_label",
        "variant": "primary",
        "action": {
          "event": {
            "name": "confirm_booking",
            "context": {
              "outboundPax": {"@path": "/outbound/pax"},
              "returnPax": {"@path": "/return/pax"}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Data message, defined by [`UpdateDataModelMessage`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "path": "/",
    "value": {
      "outbound": {"pax": 1, "price": 455},
      "return": {"pax": 2, "price": 970}
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

Surface creation message, defined by [`CreateSurfaceMessage`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage):

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v0_9/catalog.json"
  }
}
```

Layout message, defined by [`UpdateComponentsMessage`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage):

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateComponents": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "components": [
      {"id": "root", "component": "Card", "child": "layout_col"},
      {
        "id": "layout_col",
        "component": "Column",
        "children": ["flight_outbound", "flight_return", "submit_btn"]
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_outbound",
        "component": "FlightCard",
        "flightNumber": "LH 454",
        "origin": "BER",
        "destination": "SFO",
        "price": {"path": "/outbound/price"},
        "passengers": {"path": "/outbound/pax"}
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_return",
        "component": "FlightCard",
        "flightNumber": "UA 901",
        "origin": "SFO",
        "destination": "BER",
        "price": {"path": "/return/price"},
        "passengers": {"path": "/return/pax"}
      },
      {"id": "submit_label", "component": "Text", "text": "Confirm booking"},
      {
        "id": "submit_btn",
        "component": "Button",
        "child": "submit_label",
        "variant": "primary",
        "action": {
          "event": {
            "name": "confirm_booking",
            "context": {
              "outboundPax": {"path": "/outbound/pax"},
              "returnPax": {"path": "/return/pax"}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Data message, defined by [`UpdateDataModelMessage`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage):

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "path": "/",
    "value": {
      "outbound": {"pax": 1, "price": 455},
      "return": {"pax": 2, "price": 970}
    }
  }
}
```

### Render on the client

The client receives `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, and `updateDataModel` over its transport (for example AG-UI, A2A, MCP, or a WebSocket), and the A2UI Renderer:

1. Creates the surface identified by `surfaceId` and stores the initial values in its data model.
2. Resolves the flat component list and data model into a hierarchical node layer starting at `root`, following each `child` and `children` ID and binding path references (such as `/outbound/pax`) to their values in the data model.
3. Builds the native widgets from that node tree and subscribes each widget to updates on its bound properties.

At this point, the client's node layer joins the component hierarchy with the resolved values from the data model. `Card` (`root`) wraps `Column` (`layout_col`), which contains the two `FlightCard` nodes with their bound prices and passenger counts alongside `Button` (`submit_btn`) and its `Text` label:

```text
Surface ("flight-booking-surface")
└── Card ("root")
    └── Column ("layout_col")
        ├── FlightCard ("flight_outbound")
        │     flightNumber: "LH 454"
        │     origin: "BER"
        │     destination: "SFO"
        │     price: 455        ← /outbound/price
        │     passengers: 1     ← /outbound/pax
        ├── FlightCard ("flight_return")
        │     flightNumber: "UA 901"
        │     origin: "SFO"
        │     destination: "BER"
        │     price: 970        ← /return/price
        │     passengers: 2     ← /return/pax
        └── Button ("submit_btn")
            │ variant: "primary"
            │ action: event "confirm_booking"
            │   outboundPax: 1  ← /outbound/pax
            │   returnPax: 2    ← /return/pax
            └── Text ("submit_label")
                  text: "Confirm booking"
```

### Handle user actions

Once the surface is rendered, the renderer handles local state edits on the client and sends explicit user triggers back to the agent:

1. When the user taps `+` on the outbound `FlightCard` to raise the passenger count to `2`, `FlightCard` writes `2` directly to `/outbound/pax` in the surface's data model. Every node bound to `/outbound/pax` updates in place, and nothing is sent to the agent.
2. When the user taps _Confirm booking_, the renderer triggers the `Button` node's action, resolves its `context` paths against the current data model, and sends an [`action`](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) message to the agent.

The action message for this example, after the user raised the outbound count to `2`:

#### v1.0

Defined by [`renderer_to_agent.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "action": {
    "name": "confirm_booking",
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "sourceComponentId": "submit_btn",
    "timestamp": "2026-10-12T08:30:00Z",
    "context": {"outboundPax": 2, "returnPax": 2}
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

Defined by [`client_to_server.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json/properties/action):

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "action": {
    "name": "confirm_booking",
    "surfaceId": "flight-booking-surface",
    "sourceComponentId": "submit_btn",
    "timestamp": "2026-10-12T08:30:00Z",
    "context": {"outboundPax": 2, "returnPax": 2}
  }
}
```

---

# Actions, Events and Functions

> How component actions send events to the agent or trigger functions, and how A2UI functions work across actions, property bindings, validation checks, and agent requests.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/actions-and-functions/

An action defines what happens when a user interacts with a component by triggering either an [event](#events) or a [function](#functions). Events prompt the agent to respond with UI updates, while functions execute specific logic on the renderer or agent. Functions can also run outside user actions, such as property bindings, validation checks, and agent requests.

## Actions

An **action** is an interaction handler property on an interactive UI component, such as `Button.action` on [`Button`](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json/components/Button), that runs when a user interacts with that component (for example, clicking or tapping a button).

An action determines how user interaction is handled:

- An event notifies the agent of user intent by sending an outbound [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message. Use an event when the agent needs to decide what happens next and stream UI or data updates back to the client (such as confirming an order or booking a reservation).
- A function invokes a registered catalog operation directly without starting a new agent conversation turn. The function can execute locally on the renderer (such as opening a link with [`openUrl`](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json/functions/openUrl)) or run remotely on the agent via [`callAgentFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/callAgentFunction) to perform a discrete backend check (such as verifying inventory).

See [`Action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action) in the protocol schema for the action structure.

| Aspect          | Event                                             | Function                                                |
| :-------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------ |
| Action property | `action.event`                                    | `action.functionCall`                                   |
| Purpose         | Prompts the agent to process intent and update UI | Triggers specific logic on the renderer or agent        |
| Triggered by    | A user gesture on a component action              | Actions, property bindings, validation checks, or agent |
| Runs on         | The agent, after an `action` message              | The renderer, or the agent via `callAgentFunction`      |
| Agent turn      | Starts a new agent conversation turn              | Runs without starting an agent turn                     |
| Result          | The agent decides next steps and updates UI       | A typed return value, or a local side effect            |

> **Note**

In v0.9.1 ([`Action`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action)), `action.event` does not support `userMessage`, and `action.functionCall` uses `"call"` instead of `"@call"` and executes only locally on the renderer.

---

## Events

Events inform the agent that a user interacted with a component and prompt the agent to respond. When a user clicks or taps a component configured with an event (such as a "Book flight" button), the client sends an [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message to the agent. The agent processes the interaction, makes any required decisions or backend updates, and streams back updated UI components or data.

When dispatching an event, the client performs the following tasks:

1. Reads any context values attached to the event (such as the flight number or selected seat) and resolves data bindings against the current surface data model.
2. Evaluates an optional human-readable `userMessage` describing what the user did (for example, `"Confirmed flight reservation for Alex Rosario"`, formatted with [`formatString`](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json/functions/formatString)).
3. Sends an [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message to the agent containing the event name, source component, timestamp, resolved context, and optional user message.

If the surface is configured to share its data model, the client also attaches the full surface state to outbound messages so the agent has complete visibility into what the user sees. See [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/#synchronizing-state-back-to-the-agent) for details.

The following example shows a confirmation `Button` declaration and the outbound `action` message the renderer sends when the user clicks it.

#### v1.0

`Button` component declaration:

```json
{
  "id": "confirm_button",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "confirm_label",
  "variant": "primary",
  "action": {
    "event": {
      "name": "confirmReservation",
      "userMessage": {
        "@call": "formatString",
        "args": {
          "value": "Confirmed flight reservation for ${/passenger/fullName}"
        }
      },
      "context": {
        "flightNumber": "UA-402",
        "seat": {"@path": "/selection/seatNumber"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Outbound [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message sent on click:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "action": {
    "name": "confirmReservation",
    "surfaceId": "booking_surface",
    "sourceComponentId": "confirm_button",
    "timestamp": "2026-11-02T03:45:00Z",
    "userMessage": "Confirmed flight reservation for Alex Rosario",
    "context": {
      "flightNumber": "UA-402",
      "seat": "14B"
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

`Button` component declaration:

```json
{
  "id": "confirm_button",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "confirm_label",
  "variant": "primary",
  "action": {
    "event": {
      "name": "confirmReservation",
      "context": {
        "flightNumber": "UA-402",
        "seat": {"path": "/selection/seatNumber"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Outbound [`action`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json/properties/action) message sent on click:

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "action": {
    "name": "confirmReservation",
    "surfaceId": "booking_surface",
    "sourceComponentId": "confirm_button",
    "timestamp": "2026-11-02T03:45:00Z",
    "context": {
      "flightNumber": "UA-402",
      "seat": "14B"
    }
  }
}
```

> **Note**

In v0.9.1, data bindings use `path` instead of `@path`, events do not support `userMessage` (all interaction details must be provided in `context`), and client-to-server action messages are defined in [`client_to_server.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json/properties/action).

---

## Functions

Functions execute specific logic or calculations on either the client or the server. Unlike events, which start an agent turn to generate or update entire UI surfaces, functions are focused operations that compute a value, validate input, access local state, or trigger a local operation. Every available function is declared in a [catalog](/concepts/catalogs/), defining its name and expected parameters.

### Function types

Functions run either locally on the client renderer or remotely on the agent.

When evaluating a function call, the client checks whether the function is registered locally in its catalog. If a local implementation exists, the client runs it immediately without making a network request. If the function is not implemented locally, the client routes the call to the agent via [`callAgentFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/callAgentFunction) and awaits the response.

#### Renderer functions

Renderer functions are implemented locally by the client renderer and registered with its catalog. Some types of renderer functions are:

- Validation functions that check input values or form readiness against constraints, such as required fields or email formatting.
- Data transformation functions that format numbers, dates, currency, or strings, or evaluate boolean logic before displaying values on screen.
- Local data access functions that read client-side state or template context not stored in the surface data model, such as an item's position inside a list template or device screen dimensions.
- Local action functions that perform client-side operations in response to user gestures, such as opening a URL in the browser.

These examples illustrate common functions available in the [Basic Catalog](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#2-renderer-side-functions). See the [Basic Catalog functions specification](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json/functions) for the full set of standard renderer functions, or define custom functions in your own catalog.

#### Agent functions

Agent functions run on the server rather than in the client application. They let UI components trigger discrete backend operations (such as checking real-time inventory or validating a coupon code) without starting a full conversation turn.

When a component calls an agent function, the following steps occur:

1. The client sends a [`callAgentFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/callAgentFunction) request naming the function, its resolved `catalogId`, and its arguments. While waiting for the server, the client can display a pending or loading state.
2. The server executes the function logic and returns an [`agentFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/AgentFunctionResponseMessage) containing either a `value` or an `error` object.
3. The client applies the returned `value` to the component property, validation check, or action. If the call returns an error, property bindings resolve to `null` and report an [`error`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/error) message (`code: "EXPRESSION_ERROR"` with the failed `functionCallId`), validation checks mark the component as invalid, and in-progress component actions stop and report `EXPRESSION_ERROR` with `functionCallId`.

The following example shows an outbound agent function call to verify product stock:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "callAgentFunction": {
    "surfaceId": "checkout_surface",
    "functionCallId": "call_inv_check_881",
    "callFunction": {
      "@call": "checkInventory",
      "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/store/v1/catalog.json",
      "args": {
        "sku": "SKU-99201",
        "quantity": 2
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> **Note**

Any function not implemented locally by the client renderer is automatically routed to the agent. If a renderer function name is misspelled (such as `"formatCurrncy"` instead of `"formatCurrency"`), the client attempts to call it as an agent function, and the agent responds with an unknown function error.

### Calling functions

Functions can be invoked in four contexts:

- Component actions, when a user clicks or taps a component configured to execute a function directly.
- Property bindings, when a component property computes its display value from a function.
- Validation checks, when an input field or button evaluates rules before allowing user progress.
- Agent requests, when the agent asks the client to execute a local function on the device.

#### Component actions

A component action can execute a function directly instead of sending an event to the agent. For example, clicking this help button opens a support URL in the browser without contacting the agent:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "help_link",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "help_text",
  "variant": "borderless",
  "action": {
    "functionCall": {
      "@call": "openUrl",
      "args": {
        "url": "https://support.example.com/billing"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "help_link",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "help_text",
  "variant": "borderless",
  "action": {
    "functionCall": {
      "call": "openUrl",
      "args": {
        "url": "https://support.example.com/billing"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Property bindings

Component properties can compute their value from a function call. The client automatically re-evaluates the function whenever the underlying bound data changes. In this example, a text component formats an order subtotal into currency:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "order_total_text",
  "component": "Text",
  "text": {
    "@call": "formatCurrency",
    "args": {
      "value": {"@path": "/order/subtotal"},
      "currency": "USD"
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "order_total_text",
  "component": "Text",
  "text": {
    "call": "formatCurrency",
    "args": {
      "value": {"path": "/order/subtotal"},
      "currency": "USD"
    }
  }
}
```

#### Validation checks

Interactive components like text fields and buttons can define validation rules. Each rule checks a condition (such as verifying required fields or checking email format) and provides an error message if the check fails. For buttons, failing any validation check automatically disables the button:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "user_email_input",
  "component": "TextField",
  "label": "Email",
  "value": {"@path": "/formData/email"},
  "checks": [
    {
      "condition": {
        "@call": "required",
        "args": {"value": {"@path": "/formData/email"}}
      },
      "message": "Email address is required."
    },
    {
      "condition": {
        "@call": "email",
        "args": {"value": {"@path": "/formData/email"}}
      },
      "message": "Enter a valid email address."
    }
  ]
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "user_email_input",
  "component": "TextField",
  "label": "Email",
  "value": {"path": "/formData/email"},
  "checks": [
    {
      "condition": {
        "call": "required",
        "args": {"value": {"path": "/formData/email"}}
      },
      "message": "Email address is required."
    },
    {
      "condition": {
        "call": "email",
        "args": {"value": {"path": "/formData/email"}}
      },
      "message": "Enter a valid email address."
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Agent requests

The agent can also request the client to execute a function locally via [`callRendererFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CallRendererFunctionMessage), for example to query device screen dimensions. The client runs the local function and always replies with a [`rendererFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/rendererFunctionResponse) message containing the matching `functionCallId` and either `value` or `error` (even when the function's return type is `void`):

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "callRendererFunction": {
    "functionCallId": "hw_screen_001",
    "callFunction": {
      "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/device.json",
      "@call": "getScreenResolution",
      "args": {
        "screenIndex": 0
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Who can call a function

Because functions can trigger sensitive side effects (like opening a browser URL) or access device attributes, a catalog [`FunctionDefinition`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#catalog_definition.json/$defs/FunctionDefinition) can control who is permitted to call it and whether it requires a direct user gesture:

- The `allowedCallers` property restricts callers to `"rendererOnly"` (the default), `"agentOnly"`, or `"rendererOrAgent"`. For example, `"rendererOnly"` functions cannot be invoked remotely by the agent via `callRendererFunction`, while `"agentOnly"` functions can only be called by the agent and cannot be used in component properties or actions.
- The `requiresUserActivation` property (which defaults to `false` and requires `allowedCallers: "rendererOnly"` when `true`) restricts execution to a direct user tap or click on a component action, such as `openUrl`. This prevents passive property bindings, validation checks, or incoming agent messages from triggering browser navigation without user intent.

> **Note**

In v0.9.1, function calls use `call` instead of `@call` and data bindings use `path` instead of `@path`. All functions execute locally on the client renderer; v0.9.1 does not support remote agent functions, agent requests to the renderer, or caller permission settings.

---

# Catalogs

> How component catalogs define the components, functions, and rules shared between agents and renderers.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/catalogs/

An A2UI catalog defines the UI components, the functions that populate data or handle user events, and the prompt instructions that an agent and a renderer agree on. Because both sides work from the same catalog contract, the agent only sends component types and properties that the renderer knows how to build natively, never raw HTML, CSS, or executable scripts.

In the diagram below, the renderer advertises the catalogs it supports through `supportedCatalogIds`, and the agent selects a default catalog for a surface by setting `catalogId` in `createSurface`. The shared catalog document has three sections: components such as `FlightStatusCard` and `Column`, functions such as `formatCurrency` and `saveBoardingPass`, and Markdown `instructions` that the agent SDK adds to the LLM system prompt.

<CatalogAnatomy />

## Catalogs

A catalog is a collection of components and functions that acts as a contract between an agent and a renderer. Both agents and renderers can support one or more catalogs at the same time: a renderer advertises its `supportedCatalogIds` when a session starts, and an agent can create surfaces against any of those catalogs or, in v1.0, combine components and functions from multiple catalogs on the same surface by setting `catalogId` on individual entries.

Every catalog has a `catalogId` string, conventionally formatted as a URI such as `https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json` or `https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json`, along with optional `instructions`, `components`, and `functions`. Both sides of the connection read from that contract:

1. On the agent, the agent SDK (`@a2ui/agent`, `a2ui-agent-sdk`, `a2ui_agent`) reads the component schemas, function signatures, and `instructions` to build the LLM system prompt and validate outgoing messages.
2. On the renderer, the core and framework SDKs (`@a2ui/web_core`, `a2ui_core`, `A2UICore`, `androidx.a2ui`) pair each component schema with a native widget and each local function signature with code that runs on the client.

## Components

A component is a UI component that is rendered natively on the client, such as a Flutter widget, a React, Lit, or Angular component, a SwiftUI view, or a Jetpack Compose composable, and composed with other components to form rich UIs. Instead of nesting JSON objects deeply, an A2UI surface stores component instances in a flat list where parent components reference child IDs, making layouts straightforward for an LLM to stream incrementally.

Each entry in a catalog's `components` map is a JSON Schema that describes one component type:

| Part               | How it is declared                                                      | What it does                                                                                                        |
| :----------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Component type     | `"component": { "const": "FlightStatusCard" }`                          | Names the component type in the surface's flat component list.                                                      |
| Dynamic properties | `$ref` to `DynamicString`, `DynamicNumber`, `DynamicBoolean`, and so on | Accepts a literal value, a data binding (`@path` in v1.0, `path` in v0.9.1), or a function call (`@call` / `call`). |
| Children           | `$ref` to `ComponentId` or `ChildList`                                  | Points to child components by ID so the surface stays a flat list instead of a nested tree.                         |
| Placement rules    | `allowedParents`, `allowedChildren` (v1.0)                              | Limits where the component can appear in the layout.                                                                |
| Validation         | `$ref` to `Checkable`                                                   | Adds a `checks` array of `{condition, message}` rules to an input.                                                  |
| Actions            | `$ref` to `Action`                                                      | Says what happens when the user interacts with the component: send an event to the agent or call a function.        |

Here is a custom `FlightStatusCard` component schema in a catalog:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "FlightStatusCard": {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "Shows a flight's number, fare, and action buttons.",
    "allowedParents": ["Column", "List"],
    "properties": {
      "component": {"const": "FlightStatusCard"},
      "flightNumber": {
        "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
        "description": "IATA flight designator, such as 'NH 105'."
      },
      "fareAmount": {
        "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicNumber",
        "description": "Ticket fare in the booking currency."
      },
      "actions": {
        "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/ChildList",
        "description": "Buttons shown in the card footer."
      }
    },
    "required": ["component", "flightNumber"]
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "FlightStatusCard": {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "Shows a flight's number, fare, and action buttons.",
    "allOf": [
      {
        "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/ComponentCommon"
      },
      {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "component": {"const": "FlightStatusCard"},
          "flightNumber": {
            "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
            "description": "IATA flight designator, such as 'NH 105'."
          },
          "fareAmount": {
            "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicNumber",
            "description": "Ticket fare in the booking currency."
          },
          "actions": {
            "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/ChildList",
            "description": "Buttons shown in the card footer."
          }
        },
        "required": ["component", "flightNumber"]
      }
    ],
    "unevaluatedProperties": false
  }
}
```

## Functions

A function is named logic used to populate data in the UI, such as formatting a bound property or checking an input rule, or to handle user events when someone interacts with a component.

A2UI supports both renderer-side and agent-side functions:

1. Renderer-side functions are declared in a catalog's `functions` map and run locally on the client. They handle formatting, input validation, boolean logic, and client side effects such as opening a URL. In v1.0, the agent can also invoke an authorized renderer-side function remotely by sending `callRendererFunction` and reading the returned `rendererFunctionResponse`.
2. Agent-side functions, introduced in v1.0, run on the server, such as checking live seat inventory or verifying a booking code. When a component evaluates a `@call` whose name is not registered in the renderer's local catalog, the renderer treats it as an agent-side function, dispatches `callAgentFunction`, and applies the returned `agentFunctionResponse`. In v0.9.1, function calls run only on the renderer, and components notify the agent of user interactions through `action` events.

Each entry in a catalog's `functions` map declares a `returnType` (`"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`, `"array"`, `"object"`, `"any"`, `"void"`, or, in v1.0, `"validationResult"`) and an `args` schema for its arguments:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "formatCurrency": {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "Formats a number as a currency string.",
    "returnType": "string",
    "properties": {
      "@call": {"const": "formatCurrency"},
      "args": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "value": {
            "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicNumber",
            "description": "The monetary amount."
          },
          "currency": {
            "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
            "description": "The ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR')."
          }
        },
        "required": ["currency", "value"],
        "unevaluatedProperties": false
      }
    },
    "required": ["@call", "args"]
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "formatCurrency": {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "Formats a number as a currency string.",
    "properties": {
      "call": {"const": "formatCurrency"},
      "args": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "value": {
            "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicNumber",
            "description": "The monetary amount."
          },
          "currency": {
            "$ref": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString",
            "description": "The ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR')."
          }
        },
        "required": ["currency", "value"],
        "unevaluatedProperties": false
      },
      "returnType": {"const": "string"}
    },
    "required": ["call", "args"],
    "unevaluatedProperties": false
  }
}
```

## Using a catalog in an agent

An agent loads a catalog from its JSON document and passes it to `A2uiGenerator` through a `CatalogConfig`. The generator uses the catalog to build the LLM system prompt and to validate the messages the LLM produces.

#### TypeScript

```typescript
import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';

import {A2uiGenerator, CatalogConfig, ExpressFormatFactory} from '@a2ui/agent';
import {Catalog} from '@a2ui/web_core';

const travelCatalog = Catalog.fromJson(JSON.parse(readFileSync('./catalogs/travel.json', 'utf8')));

const generator = new A2uiGenerator(
  [new CatalogConfig(travelCatalog)],
  undefined,
  new ExpressFormatFactory(),
);
```

#### Python

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

from a2ui.core import Catalog
from a2ui.inference_formats import ExpressFormatFactory
from a2ui.processor import A2uiGenerator, CatalogConfig

travel_catalog = Catalog.from_json(
    json.loads(Path("./catalogs/travel.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
)

generator = A2uiGenerator(
    catalogs=[CatalogConfig(catalog=travel_catalog)],
    inference_format_factory=ExpressFormatFactory(),
)
```

#### Dart

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:a2ui_agent/a2ui_agent.dart';
import 'package:a2ui_core/a2ui_core.dart';

void main() {
  final travelCatalog = Catalog.fromJson(
    jsonDecode(File('./catalogs/travel.json').readAsStringSync())
        as Map<String, Object?>,
  );

  final generator = A2uiGenerator(
    catalogs: [CatalogConfig(travelCatalog)],
    inferenceFormatFactory: const ExpressFormatFactory(),
  );
}
```

Swift (`A2UISwiftCore`, `A2UISwiftUI`) and Kotlin (`androidx.a2ui`, `androidx.a2ui.compose`) target client-side rendering; see [SDKs](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) for server-side Agent SDK packages.

## Registering a catalog in a renderer

A renderer builds a `Catalog` that pairs each component schema with a native widget (`ComponentImplementation`) and each local function signature with code that runs it (`FunctionImplementation`). It then passes the catalog to its message processor or framework provider.

#### Flutter

```dart
import 'package:a2ui_core/a2ui_core.dart';
import 'package:a2ui_flutter/a2ui_flutter.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:json_schema_builder/json_schema_builder.dart';

final flightStatusCard = ComponentImplementation(
  name: 'FlightStatusCard',
  allowedParents: ['Column', 'List'],
  schema: Schema.object(
    properties: {
      'component': Schema.string(enumValues: ['FlightStatusCard']),
      'flightNumber': CommonSchemasV1.dynamicString,
      'fareAmount': CommonSchemasV1.dynamicNumber,
    },
    required: ['component', 'flightNumber'],
  ),
  builder: (context, node, props, buildChild) {
    final flightNumber = props.string('flightNumber') ?? '';
    final fare = props.number('fareAmount');

    return Card(
      child: ListTile(
        leading: const Icon(Icons.flight_takeoff),
        title: Text('Flight $flightNumber'),
        trailing: fare != null ? Text('\$${fare.toStringAsFixed(2)}') : null,
      ),
    );
  },
);

final travelCatalog = Catalog<ComponentImplementation, FunctionImplementation>(
  id: 'https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json',
  protocolVersion: A2uiProtocolVersion.v1_0,
  components: [flightStatusCard],
  functions: BasicCatalog.v1_0().functions.values.toList(),
);

final processor = MessageProcessor(catalogs: [travelCatalog]);
```

#### React

```tsx
import {z} from 'zod';

import {createComponentImplementation} from '@a2ui/react';
import {Catalog, type ComponentApi, MessageProcessor} from '@a2ui/web_core';
import {BASIC_FUNCTIONS, DynamicNumberSchema, DynamicStringSchema} from '@a2ui/web_core/v1_0';

const FlightStatusCardApi = {
  name: 'FlightStatusCard',
  allowedParents: ['Column', 'List'],
  schema: z.object({
    flightNumber: DynamicStringSchema,
    fareAmount: DynamicNumberSchema.optional(),
  }),
} satisfies ComponentApi;

const FlightStatusCard = createComponentImplementation(FlightStatusCardApi, ({props}) => {
  const flightNumber = typeof props.flightNumber === 'string' ? props.flightNumber : '';
  const fareAmount = typeof props.fareAmount === 'number' ? props.fareAmount : undefined;

  return (
    <div className="flight-card">
      <strong>Flight {flightNumber}</strong>
      {fareAmount !== undefined && <span>${fareAmount.toFixed(2)}</span>}
    </div>
  );
});

export const travelCatalog = new Catalog(
  'https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json',
  '1.0',
  [FlightStatusCard],
  BASIC_FUNCTIONS,
);

const processor = new MessageProcessor([travelCatalog]);
```

#### Lit

```typescript
import {html, nothing} from 'lit';
import {customElement} from 'lit/decorators.js';
import {z} from 'zod';

import {A2uiLitElement, type LitComponentApi} from '@a2ui/lit';
import {Catalog, type ComponentApi, MessageProcessor} from '@a2ui/web_core';
import {BASIC_FUNCTIONS, DynamicNumberSchema, DynamicStringSchema} from '@a2ui/web_core/v1_0';

const FlightStatusCardApi = {
  name: 'FlightStatusCard',
  allowedParents: ['Column', 'List'],
  schema: z.object({
    flightNumber: DynamicStringSchema,
    fareAmount: DynamicNumberSchema.optional(),
  }),
} satisfies ComponentApi;

@customElement('flight-status-card')
export class FlightStatusCardElement extends A2uiLitElement<typeof FlightStatusCardApi> {
  static readonly tagName = 'flight-status-card';
  protected override readonly api = FlightStatusCardApi;

  override render() {
    const rawFlight = this.controller?.props?.flightNumber;
    const rawFare = this.controller?.props?.fareAmount;
    const flightNumber = typeof rawFlight === 'string' ? rawFlight : '';
    const fareAmount = typeof rawFare === 'number' ? rawFare : undefined;

    return html`
      <div class="flight-card">
        <strong>Flight ${flightNumber}</strong>
        ${fareAmount !== undefined ? html`<span>$${fareAmount.toFixed(2)}</span>` : nothing}
      </div>
    `;
  }
}

const FlightStatusCard = {
  ...FlightStatusCardApi,
  tagName: FlightStatusCardElement.tagName,
  element: FlightStatusCardElement,
} satisfies LitComponentApi;

export const travelCatalog = new Catalog(
  'https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json',
  '1.0',
  [FlightStatusCard],
  BASIC_FUNCTIONS,
);

const processor = new MessageProcessor([travelCatalog]);
```

#### Angular

```typescript
import {Component, computed} from '@angular/core';
import {z} from 'zod';

import {
  AngularCatalog,
  BASIC_FUNCTIONS,
  CatalogComponent,
  createComponentImplementation,
  provideA2UI,
} from '@a2ui/angular';
import {type ComponentApi} from '@a2ui/web_core';
import {DynamicNumberSchema, DynamicStringSchema} from '@a2ui/web_core/v1_0';

const FlightStatusCardApi = {
  name: 'FlightStatusCard',
  allowedParents: ['Column', 'List'],
  schema: z.object({
    flightNumber: DynamicStringSchema,
    fareAmount: DynamicNumberSchema.optional(),
  }),
} satisfies ComponentApi;

@Component({
  selector: 'app-flight-status-card',
  template: `
    <div class="flight-card">
      <strong>Flight {{ flightNumber() }}</strong>
      @if (formattedFare(); as fare) {
        <span>\${{ fare }}</span>
      }
    </div>
  `,
})
export class FlightStatusCardComponent extends CatalogComponent<typeof FlightStatusCardApi> {
  readonly flightNumber = computed(() => {
    const flight = this.props().flightNumber?.value();
    return typeof flight === 'string' ? flight : '';
  });
  readonly formattedFare = computed(() => {
    const fare = this.props().fareAmount?.value();
    return typeof fare === 'number' ? fare.toFixed(2) : undefined;
  });
}

export const travelCatalog = new AngularCatalog(
  'https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json',
  '1.0',
  [createComponentImplementation(FlightStatusCardApi, FlightStatusCardComponent)],
  BASIC_FUNCTIONS,
);

export const appA2uiProviders = provideA2UI({catalogs: [travelCatalog]});
```

#### SwiftUI

```swift
import A2UICore
import A2UISwiftUI
import BasicCatalog
import JSONSchema
import SwiftUI

let flightStatusCard = ComponentImplementation(
  name: "FlightStatusCard",
  schema: try! Schema(
    instance: """
      {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "component": { "const": "FlightStatusCard" },
          "flightNumber": { "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicString" },
          "fareAmount": { "$ref": "common_types.json#/$defs/DynamicNumber" }
        },
        "required": ["component", "flightNumber"]
      }
      """,
    remoteSchemas: A2UICommonSchema.allSchemas
  ),
  allowedParents: ["Column", "List"]
) { node in
  HStack {
    Image(systemName: "airplane.departure")
    Text("Flight \(node.string(for: "flightNumber") ?? "")")
      .font(.headline)
    Spacer()
    if let fare = node.double(for: "fareAmount") {
      Text(String(format: "$%.2f", fare))
    }
  }
  .padding()
}

let travelCatalog = Catalog(
  id: "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json",
  protocolVersion: "1.0",
  components: [flightStatusCard],
  functions: V10BasicFunctions.allFunctions
)

let processor = MessageProcessor(catalogs: [travelCatalog])
```

#### Jetpack Compose

```kotlin
import android.content.Context
import java.util.Locale

import androidx.a2ui.compose.runtime.A2uiComponentProperties
import androidx.a2ui.compose.runtime.A2uiComponentScope
import androidx.a2ui.compose.runtime.A2uiMessageProcessor
import androidx.a2ui.compose.runtime.A2uiProperty
import androidx.a2ui.compose.ui.A2uiCatalog
import androidx.a2ui.compose.ui.A2uiComponent
import androidx.a2ui.compose.ui.catalog.A2uiBasicCatalogV1
import androidx.a2ui.model.processor.A2uiMessageProcessor
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.material3.a2ui.catalog.MaterialA2uiBasicCatalogV1Defaults
import androidx.compose.material3.a2ui.catalog.materialA2uiBasicCatalogV1
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp

private val FlightNumberProp =
    A2uiProperty.dynamicString("flightNumber", required = true)
private val FareAmountProp =
    A2uiProperty.dynamicNumber("fareAmount")

val FlightStatusCard: A2uiComponent =
    object : A2uiComponent {
        override val name = "FlightStatusCard"
        override val description = "Shows a flight's number and fare."
        override val properties = listOf(FlightNumberProp, FareAmountProp)

        @Composable
        override fun A2uiComponentScope.isReady(properties: A2uiComponentProperties): Boolean =
            properties.bind(FlightNumberProp) != null

        @Composable
        override fun A2uiComponentScope.Content(
            properties: A2uiComponentProperties,
            modifier: Modifier,
        ) {
            val flightNumber = properties.bind(FlightNumberProp) ?: return
            val fare = properties.bind(FareAmountProp)?.toDouble()

            Card(modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
                Row(
                    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp),
                    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
                ) {
                    Text(text = "Flight $flightNumber")
                    if (fare != null) {
                        Text(text = String.format(Locale.US, "$%.2f", fare))
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

// androidx.a2ui implements v0.9.1, where each surface binds to a single catalogId.
fun createTravelProcessor(context: Context): A2uiMessageProcessor {
    val basicCatalog =
        materialA2uiBasicCatalogV1(
            image = MaterialA2uiBasicCatalogV1Defaults.image { _, _, _, _, _ -> },
            video = MaterialA2uiBasicCatalogV1Defaults.video { _, _, _ -> },
            audioPlayer = MaterialA2uiBasicCatalogV1Defaults.audioPlayer { _, _, _, _ -> },
            functions = A2uiBasicCatalogV1.Functions(context),
        )
    val travelCatalog =
        A2uiCatalog(
            catalogId = "https://example.com/catalogs/travel/v1/catalog.json",
            components = basicCatalog.components + FlightStatusCard,
            functions = basicCatalog.functions,
            themeSchema = basicCatalog.themeSchema,
        )
    // Launch processor.collectMessages() in a background coroutine scope
    // (such as viewModelScope) to process queued messages:
    val processor = A2uiMessageProcessor(catalogs = listOf(travelCatalog))
    return processor
}
```

## The basic catalog

A2UI publishes a basic catalog with 18 general-purpose components and 14 functions. The v1.0 schema lives at [`catalogs/basic/v1/catalog.json`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/catalogs/basic/v1/catalog.json), and the v0.9.1 schema lives at [`specification/v0_9_1/catalogs/basic/catalog.json`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/specification/v0_9_1/catalogs/basic/catalog.json).

| Category          | Entries                                                                                                                                                       |
| :---------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Layout            | `Row`, `Column`, `List`, `Card`, `Tabs`, `Modal`, `Divider`                                                                                                   |
| Display and media | `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Video`, `AudioPlayer`                                                                                                               |
| Inputs            | `Button`, `TextField`, `CheckBox`, `ChoicePicker`, `Slider`, `DateTimeInput`                                                                                  |
| Functions         | `formatString`, `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `pluralize`, `required`, `regex`, `length`, `numeric`, `email`, `openUrl`, `and`, `or`, `not` |

You do not have to use the basic catalog. You can adopt it as is, restyle its components to match your design system, combine it with domain-specific catalogs on the same surface, or replace it altogether.

## Catalog negotiation and multi-catalog surfaces

When a session starts, the renderer sends `supportedCatalogIds` to list the catalogs it supports. When creating a surface, the agent picks from that list (or sends no UI if none match).

#### v1.0

Set `catalogId` in `createSurface` to choose the surface's default catalog, then add `catalogId` on any component in `updateComponents` or function call (`@call`) that comes from another supported catalog.

In this example, `salesDashboard` uses the basic catalog by default, and `chart` comes from a custom charts catalog:

```json
[
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "createSurface": {
      "surfaceId": "salesDashboard",
      "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "salesDashboard",
      "components": [
        {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["title", "chart"]},
        {"id": "title", "component": "Text", "text": "Quarterly sales"},
        {
          "id": "chart",
          "component": "BarChart",
          "catalogId": "https://example.com/catalogs/charts/v1/catalog.json",
          "data": {"@path": "/sales"}
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

<details>
<summary>Edge cases when <code>createSurface.catalogId</code> is omitted</summary>

`catalogId` in `createSurface` is optional. If a surface omits `createSurface.catalogId`, every component and function call on that surface must set its own `catalogId`. If an entry omits `catalogId` and the surface has no default `catalogId` either, the renderer rejects that component or function call rather than falling back to `supportedCatalogIds`. See [Mixable catalogs and component resolution logic](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#mixable-catalogs-and-component-resolution-logic) for the full resolution rules.

</details>

#### v0.9.1

The agent selects a single `catalogId` in `createSurface`, locked for the lifetime of that surface:

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "salesDashboard",
    "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"
  }
}
```

---

# Data Model and Data Binding

> Learn how A2UI separates surface UI structure from reactive JSON state, enabling dynamic display bindings, two-way input bindings, dynamic list templates, and state synchronization back to the agent.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/data-binding/

A2UI separates UI component structure from runtime data by giving every surface an isolated JSON data model and binding components to paths within that model.

Components reference locations inside the data model using [RFC 6901 JSON Pointers](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901) (such as `/reservation/destination` or `/reservation/guestEmail`). When either the agent or the user updates a path in the data model, only the components bound to that path update.

The following diagram shows how a surface data model and component bindings produce a rendered UI. On the left, the surface data model stores reservation state in JSON, and component definitions bind to paths such as `/reservation/destination` and `/reservation/guestEmail`. On the right, an application window renders the resulting interface: a heading displaying the destination, an editable text field bound two-way to the guest email, and a confirmation button.

<DataBindingAnatomy />

---

## Populating the data model

Each surface maintains its own JSON data model. In v1.0, you can provide an initial `dataModel` object inline when sending [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage), or populate and update the data model at any time by sending [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) messages (in v0.9.1, data is always sent via [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) after creating the surface).

When the renderer receives an `updateDataModel` message, it applies upsert semantics at the target JSON Pointer `path`. If the path does not exist yet, the renderer creates any missing intermediate objects and inserts the value; if the path already exists, the renderer replaces the value at that path. Omitting `path` (or setting it to `"/"`) replaces the entire root data model for the surface. To delete a key at `path`, set `"value": null` in v1.0, or omit the `value` property in v0.9.1.

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "path": "/reservation/destination",
    "value": "Kyoto, Japan"
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "path": "/reservation/destination",
    "value": "Kyoto, Japan"
  }
}
```

Because `updateDataModel` is separate from component layout messages ([`updateComponents`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage)), the data model can be updated directly by the language model during generation, or from deterministic code on the agent side (such as a tool handler or backend service injecting database records or API responses directly into the surface without passing them through the model).

---

## Binding to the data model

UI components can be bound to paths in the surface data model so they can display and update data. Component properties typed as dynamic values (such as [`DynamicString`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DynamicString), [`DynamicNumber`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DynamicNumber), [`DynamicBoolean`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DynamicBoolean), [`DynamicStringList`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DynamicStringList), or [`DynamicValue`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DynamicValue)) accept either a static literal value or a [`DataBinding`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DataBinding) object (`{"@path": "/path"}` in v1.0, or `{"path": "/path"}` in v0.9.1). Dynamic properties can also evaluate functions, which are covered in [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/).

### Reading data as dynamic values

To display a value from the data model, bind a component's dynamic property to a JSON Pointer path. Whenever the value at that path is populated or updated, the component updates automatically:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "destinationText",
  "component": "Text",
  "text": {"@path": "/reservation/destination"}
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "destinationText",
  "component": "Text",
  "text": {"path": "/reservation/destination"}
}
```

### Two-way binding to dynamic values
