Interactive input components (such as `TextField`, `CheckBox`, or `Slider`) bind their `value` property to a path in the data model. This creates a two-way binding: the input displays the current value at that path, and as the user types or toggles the control, the renderer updates that path in the local data model immediately:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "emailInput",
  "component": "TextField",
  "label": "Guest Email",
  "value": {"@path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "emailInput",
  "component": "TextField",
  "label": "Guest Email",
  "value": {"path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
}
```

### Referencing the data model in events

Component events ([`action.event`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action)) can include data model references inside their `context` object. When the user triggers the event (for example, by clicking a button to submit a form), the renderer resolves each path against the local data model and sends the current values in the outbound [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "submitButton",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "submitLabel",
  "action": {
    "event": {
      "name": "submit_reservation",
      "context": {
        "email": {"@path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "id": "submitButton",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "submitLabel",
  "action": {
    "event": {
      "name": "submit_reservation",
      "context": {
        "email": {"path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Displaying dynamic lists of data

Container components whose `children` property uses [`ChildList`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/ChildList) (such as `Column`, `Row`, or `List`) can either take a static array of child component IDs (`["item1", "item2"]`) or generate children dynamically from a list in the data model using a template object with `path` and `componentId` (`ChildList` uses the property name `"path"` in both v1.0 and v0.9.1).

When a container binds to a list path (such as `"/guests"`), the renderer repeats the template component once for each item in the array and creates a local data scope for that item:

1. A **local data model path** omits the leading slash (such as `{"@path": "name"}` in v1.0, or `{"path": "name"}` in v0.9.1) and resolves relative to the current list item. For the first item in `"/guests"`, `"name"` resolves to `"/guests/0/name"`, and for the second item, it resolves to `"/guests/1/name"`.
2. A **root data model path** starts with a leading slash (such as `{"@path": "/reservation/destination"}`) and always resolves from the root of the surface data model, even inside a list template.
3. In v1.0, the **`@index` system function** (`{"@call": "@index"}`, with an optional `"args": {"offset": 1}`) returns the current item's 0-based index inside a list template.

The following example populates a `/guests` list in the data model and renders each guest's `name` using a `Column` template:

#### v1.0

```json
[
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "booking",
      "path": "/guests",
      "value": [{"name": "Alex Rivera"}, {"name": "Sam Taylor"}]
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "booking",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": {
            "path": "/guests",
            "componentId": "guestRow"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "guestRow",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"@path": "name"}
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
[
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "booking",
      "path": "/guests",
      "value": [{"name": "Alex Rivera"}, {"name": "Sam Taylor"}]
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "booking",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": {
            "path": "/guests",
            "componentId": "guestRow"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "guestRow",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"path": "name"}
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

The following diagram shows how the `/guests` array and the `guestRow` template expand into a rendered list UI. On the left, the `/guests` array holds two objects and `guestRow` binds its text to the local path `"name"`. On the right, an application window renders two list items resolved from `/guests/0/name` and `/guests/1/name`.

<CollectionScopeDiagram />

---

## Synchronizing state back to the agent

When a user edits an input component, two-way bindings update the surface data model locally on the client without streaming every keystroke over the network. To synchronize data model state back to the agent, especially values updated by input components, you can use three mechanisms depending on how the data will be processed.

### Events

Include data model references in `action.event.context` to send specific values (such as form fields) when the user triggers an [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) event. When the user clicks the `submitButton` component shown earlier, the renderer resolves each bound path against the local data model and sends the resolved `action` message to the agent. This is best when you want to send data model state to an agent to reason over and process:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "action": {
    "name": "submit_reservation",
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "sourceComponentId": "submitButton",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-15T14:30:00Z",
    "context": {
      "email": "alex@example.com"
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "action": {
    "name": "submit_reservation",
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "sourceComponentId": "submitButton",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-15T14:30:00Z",
    "context": {
      "email": "alex@example.com"
    }
  }
}
```

### Agent functions

In v1.0, an interactive component such as a submit button can use `action.functionCall` to trigger an agent-side function (`callAgentFunction`) with arguments bound to paths in the data model. This is best when you want to send data model state directly to programmatic code on the agent side:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "id": "saveButton",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "saveLabel",
  "action": {
    "functionCall": {
      "@call": "saveReservation",
      "args": {
        "email": {"@path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

Agent-side functions were introduced in v1.0. In v0.9.1, pass bound data model paths in `action.event.context` instead:

```json
{
  "id": "saveButton",
  "component": "Button",
  "child": "saveLabel",
  "action": {
    "event": {
      "name": "save_reservation",
      "context": {
        "email": {"path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### `sendDataModel: true`

Set `"sendDataModel": true` in the [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage) message to instruct the renderer to attach the full surface data model to the transport metadata of every outbound message (`a2uiRendererDataModel` in v1.0, or `a2uiClientDataModel` in v0.9.1, shaped as `{"version": "1.0", "surfaces": {"booking": {...}}}`). This is best when you want to synchronize complete surface state as context for the agent:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
    "sendDataModel": true
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "booking",
    "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
    "sendDataModel": true
  }
}
```

---

## Accessing the data model across SDKs

Each Core SDK provides a `dataModel` interface on the surface model for reading values by JSON Pointer path:

#### TypeScript

```typescript
const surface = processor.model.getSurface('booking');
const email = surface?.dataModel.get('/reservation/guestEmail');
```

#### Python

```python
surface = processor.model.get_surface("booking")
email = surface.data_model.get("/reservation/guestEmail") if surface else None
```

#### Dart

```dart
final surface = processor.model.getSurface('booking');
final email = surface?.dataModel.get('/reservation/guestEmail');
```

#### Swift

```swift
let surface = processor.surfaceGroupModel["booking"]
let email = surface?.dataModel.get("/reservation/guestEmail")
```

#### Kotlin

```kotlin
import androidx.a2ui.engine.model.A2uiCoreSurfaceModel
import androidx.a2ui.model.protocol.A2uiDataPath

// Accessing the data model directly requires the androidx.a2ui:a2ui-engine
// dependency (which provides A2uiCoreSurfaceModel and A2uiCoreDataModel).
// Surface instances emitted by A2uiMessageProcessor implement A2uiCoreSurfaceModel:
val surface =
    processor.activeSurfaces.value.firstOrNull { it.id == "booking" } as? A2uiCoreSurfaceModel
val email = surface?.dataModel?.get(A2uiDataPath("/reservation/guestEmail"))
```

---

# Glossary

> Alphabetical reference of A2UI protocol, SDK, and generative UI terminology.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/glossary/

A2UI (Agent to User Interface) uses specific terms for its wire protocol, client and server SDKs, and generative UI patterns, defined below in alphabetical order.

[A](#a) · [B](#b) · [C](#c) · [D](#d) · [E](#e) · [F](#f) · [G](#g) · [I](#i) · [M](#m) · [N](#n) · [P](#p) · [R](#r) · [S](#s)

<span id="a2ui-protocol-terms"></span>
<span id="a2ui-agent-terms"></span>
<span id="generative-ui-terms"></span>

## A

### A2UI

**Agent to User Interface**, an open, platform-agnostic streaming UI protocol and SDK suite that lets [agents](#agent) generate stateful, native user interfaces across web, mobile, and desktop [renderers](#renderer) without sending executable code, HTML, or CSS over the wire.

See [Overview: How A2UI Works](/concepts/overview/) and the [v1.0 Protocol Specification](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/).

### A2UI message

A single JSON envelope exchanged between an [agent](#agent) and a [renderer](#renderer) over a streaming or request-response transport.

Messages flow in two directions: [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) envelopes create or delete [surfaces](#surface), update [components](#component) and [data models](#data-model), invoke renderer functions, and return agent function results; [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) envelopes dispatch user [events](#event), invoke agent functions, return renderer function results, and report validation or runtime errors. Because A2UI supports progressive delivery over streaming transports, a message stream may be in progress, completed, or interrupted if transport delivery stops early.

See [Messages](/concepts/messages/).

### A2UI tag

A delimiter tag in model-to-agent text output, such as `<a2ui>...</a2ui>` (used by the Express [inference format](#inference-format)) or `<a2ui-json>...</a2ui-json>` (used by the Direct JSON format), that marks the start and end of a structured UI block.

Because a single model response can interleave conversational prose with one or more UI blocks, the [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) parser scans for A2UI tags to separate prose from raw UI blocks before compiling those blocks into [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) messages.

See [Inference Formats](/concepts/inference-formats/).

### A2uiGenerator

The top-level coordinator class in an [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) that holds the agent's supported `CatalogConfig` entries, optional prompt examples, and default [inference format](#inference-format) factory (`ExpressFormatFactory` by default).

For each session or request, calling `createProcessor` (in TypeScript and Dart) or `create_processor` (in Python) with the renderer's [capabilities](#capabilities) negotiates the active [catalogs](#catalog) and returns an `A2uiRequestProcessor` that generates system prompt instructions and parses and validates model responses against `RendererState`.

See [Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) and [How to Integrate A2UI into an Agent](/guides/agent-integration/).

### Action

An interaction handler property on a UI [component](#component) (such as `Button.action`), defined by [`common_types.json#/$defs/Action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action) in v1.0 and [`common_types.json#/$defs/Action`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action) in v0.9.1.

An `Action` is a `oneOf` union that specifies one of two behaviors when a user interacts with the component:

1. An [`event`](#event) (`{"event": {"name": "...", "context": {...}}}`), which causes the renderer to resolve any bound values and send an outbound [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message in [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) to notify the agent of user intent.
2. A [`functionCall`](#function-call) (`{"functionCall": {"@call": "...", "args": {...}}}` in v1.0, or `"call"` in v0.9.1), which invokes a [function](#function) without dispatching an `action` event message (in v1.0, running locally on the renderer or routing to the agent via [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) when unimplemented locally).

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [Defining actions](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#defining-actions) in the protocol specification.

### Agent

<span id="a2ui-agent-and-a2ui-renderer"></span>
<span id="agent-architecture"></span>

The application or service that emits [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) messages to build and update UI [surfaces](#surface) on a [renderer](#renderer), and processes inbound [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) events and remote function calls.

To decide what UI and data to emit, an agent typically calls a large language model (LLM), coordinates specialized subagents behind an orchestrator, or runs deterministic application logic (for example, in regulated workflows or automated tests). An agent can run on a server over transports such as AG-UI, Agent-to-Agent (A2A), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Server-Sent Events (SSE), or WebSockets, or inside the same client process as the renderer. Agents may be stateful (retaining negotiated [catalogs](#catalog) and `RendererState` across turns) or stateless (receiving renderer [capabilities](#capabilities) and surface [data model](#data-model) metadata on every request).

See [Overview: How A2UI Works](/concepts/overview/) and [How to Integrate A2UI into an Agent](/guides/agent-integration/).

### Agent SDK

A first-party agent-side library (published for TypeScript, Python, and Dart on top of each language's [Core SDK](#core-sdk)) that manages an [agent](#agent)'s interaction with language models and [renderers](#renderer).

An Agent SDK loads and prunes [catalogs](#catalog) via [catalog transformers](#catalog-transformer), negotiates renderer [capabilities](#capabilities) through [`A2uiGenerator`](#a2uigenerator), generates model skills and system prompt snippets, compiles [inference format](#inference-format) output into wire JSON, and validates payloads against `RendererState` so errors can be fed back to the model for self-correction.

See [Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) for official package names and capabilities.

### agent_to_renderer

The v1.0 protocol [envelope schema](#envelope-schema) ([`agent_to_renderer.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json)) for messages streamed or returned from an [agent](#agent) to a [renderer](#renderer). In v0.9.1, this envelope schema is named [`server_to_client.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json).

Every v1.0 `agent_to_renderer` message sets `"version": "1.0"` (v0.9.1 uses `"version": "v0.9"` or `"v0.9.1"`) alongside one of six message keys:

1. [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage) initializes a new [surface](#surface) (and in v1.0 can embed initial `components` and `dataModel` inline).
2. [`updateComponents`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage) adds or replaces [component](#component) definitions in a surface's flat component list.
3. [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) inserts, replaces, or deletes (`"value": null` in v1.0; omitted `value` in v0.9.1) data at a JSON Pointer path in a surface's [data model](#data-model).
4. [`deleteSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/DeleteSurfaceMessage) removes a surface and its associated state.
5. [`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction) (new in v1.0) invokes an authorized renderer-side [function](#function).
6. [`agentFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/AgentFunctionResponseMessage) (new in v1.0) returns the `value` or `error` for a [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) request.

See [Messages](/concepts/messages/) and [Envelope message structure](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#envelope-message-structure) in the protocol specification.

### Agent turn

The sequence of [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) messages (and any accompanying conversational text) sent by an [agent](#agent) in response to a user prompt or [`Event`](#event) before the agent waits for the next user input. The end of an agent turn is signaled by the transport layer rather than by an A2UI message.

See [Messages](/concepts/messages/) and [Transport decoupling](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#transport-decoupling) in the protocol specification.

## B

### Basic catalog

The optional, general-purpose reference [catalog](#catalog) maintained by the A2UI project (`https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json` in v1.0, [`basic_catalog.json`](/specification/v1.0-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json); `https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json` in v0.9.1, [`basic_catalog.json`](/specification/v0.9.1-basic-catalog-implementation-guide/#basic_catalog.json)).

The Basic catalog defines 18 standard [components](#component) (`Row`, `Column`, `List`, `Card`, `Tabs`, `Modal`, `Divider`, `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Video`, `AudioPlayer`, `Button`, `TextField`, `CheckBox`, `ChoicePicker`, `Slider`, and `DateTimeInput`) and 14 [functions](#function) (`formatString`, `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency`, `formatDate`, `pluralize`, `required`, `regex`, `length`, `numeric`, `email`, `openUrl`, `and`, `or`, and `not`). Official [framework adapters](#framework-adapter) ship with a built-in implementation that applications can restyle, combine with custom domain catalogs, or replace altogether.

See [Catalogs](/concepts/catalogs/#the-basic-catalog) and [Basic Component Catalog](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#basic-component-catalog) in the protocol specification.

## C

### @call

The reserved v1.0 protocol directive key in a [`FunctionCall`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/FunctionCall) object that names the catalog or system [function](#function) to invoke, for example `{"@call": "formatCurrency", "args": {"value": {"@path": "/price"}, "currency": "USD"}}`.

In v0.9.1, `FunctionCall` uses `"call"` without the `@` prefix ([`common_types.json#/$defs/FunctionCall`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/FunctionCall)). Reserving the `@` prefix in v1.0 keeps plain JSON objects that have a `"call"` property from being treated as function calls; literal keys beginning with `@` inside `DynamicValue` objects are escaped by doubling the prefix (`"@@call"`).

See [Function call](#function-call), [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/), and [Functions](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#functions) in the protocol specification.

### callAgentFunction

<span id="agentfunctionresponse"></span>

A v1.0 [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) message ([`renderer_to_agent.json#/properties/callAgentFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/callAgentFunction)) sent by a [renderer](#renderer) to execute an agent-side [function](#function) remotely, such as checking live inventory or verifying an identifier.

When the renderer resolves a [`FunctionCall`](#function-call)'s [catalog](#catalog) and finds no local implementation (provided the function is not an `@`-prefixed system function, is not declared `allowedCallers: "agentOnly"`, and passes any `requiresUserActivation` and declared argument schema checks), it sends `callAgentFunction` with `surfaceId`, a unique `functionCallId`, and `callFunction` (`@call`, the resolved `catalogId`, and evaluated `args`). The [agent](#agent) runs the function and replies with an [`agentFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/AgentFunctionResponseMessage) carrying the same `functionCallId` and either `value` or `error`. Not present in v0.9.1, where functions run only on the renderer.

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [`callAgentFunction`](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#callagentfunction) in the protocol specification.

### callRendererFunction

<span id="rendererfunctionresponse"></span>

A v1.0 [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) message ([`agent_to_renderer.json#/$defs/CallRendererFunctionMessage`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CallRendererFunctionMessage)) sent by an [agent](#agent) to execute a [function](#function) registered on the [renderer](#renderer), such as reading client state or triggering an authorized client operation.

The message carries a unique `functionCallId`, an optional `surfaceId` whose [data model](#data-model) provides the evaluation context (defaulting to an isolated empty root model `{}` when omitted), and `callFunction` with `@call`, a required `catalogId`, and optional `args`. Only functions declared with `allowedCallers` set to `"agentOnly"` or `"rendererOrAgent"` (and not requiring user activation) may be called by the agent. After executing or rejecting a well-formed call, the renderer returns a [`rendererFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/rendererFunctionResponse) with the matching `functionCallId` and either `value` or `error` (malformed envelopes report a top-level [`error`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/error) message carrying `functionCallId`). Not present in v0.9.1.

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [`callRendererFunction`](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#callrendererfunction) in the protocol specification.

### Capabilities

<span id="capabilities-object"></span>

Metadata payloads exchanged via transport handshakes or per-message transport metadata (rather than as [A2UI messages](#a2ui-message)) that advertise which [catalogs](#catalog) each side supports:

1. Renderer capabilities ([`renderer_capabilities.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_capabilities.json), sent under the `a2uiRendererCapabilities` metadata key in v1.0; [`client_capabilities.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_capabilities.json) under `a2uiClientCapabilities` in v0.9.1) declare `supportedCatalogIds` and optional `inlineCatalogs` nested under the protocol version key (`"1.0"` in v1.0, `"v0.9"` in v0.9.1).
2. Agent capabilities ([`agent_capabilities.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_capabilities.json) in v1.0; [`server_capabilities.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_capabilities.json) in v0.9.1) declare the agent's `supportedCatalogIds` and `acceptsInlineCatalogs` flag.

See [Overview: How A2UI Works](/concepts/overview/) and [Capabilities and metadata](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#capabilities-and-metadata) in the protocol specification.

### Catalog

A versioned JSON Schema document ([`catalog_definition.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#catalog_definition.json)) identified by a unique `catalogId` string (conventionally formatted as a URI) that defines the UI [components](#component), [functions](#function), and Markdown `instructions` shared between an [agent](#agent) and a [renderer](#renderer).

A catalog is an explicit allowlist: the agent uses it to construct model prompts and validate generated messages, while the renderer binds each declared component to a native UI widget and each local function to client code. Catalogs can define low-level primitives (such as `Row`, `Text`, and `Button` in the [Basic catalog](#basic-catalog)) or domain-specific components (such as `FlightSelector` or `HotelCheckout`). In v1.0, a single [surface](#surface) can mix components and functions from multiple catalogs by setting `catalogId` on individual entries.

See [Catalogs](/concepts/catalogs/), [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/), and [The component catalog](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#the-component-catalog) in the protocol specification.

### Catalog transformer

<span id="why-catalog-transformers-are-needed"></span>
<span id="example-catalog-transformers"></span>

An [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) interface (`CatalogTransformer`) that filters or adapts a [catalog](#catalog) before prompt instructions are generated and validation schemas are compiled.

Pruning unused components and functions lowers prompt token consumption and restricts what UI capabilities a model can emit for a specific task or user role. Built-in implementations in the TypeScript, Python, and Dart Agent SDKs include `ComponentPruningTransformer` (which keeps an allowlist of component names) and `FunctionPruningTransformer` (which keeps an allowlist of function names). For server-side composite component expansion, see [`MacroExpander`](#macroexpander).

See [Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk).

### CheckRule

<span id="validationresult"></span>

A client-side validation rule ([`common_types.json#/$defs/CheckRule`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/CheckRule) in v1.0; [`common_types.json#/$defs/CheckRule`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/CheckRule) in v0.9.1) attached to input and interactive [components](#component) that include [`Checkable`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Checkable) (`checks`).

In v1.0, each `CheckRule` pairs a `condition` (a [`DataBinding`](#data-binding) or [`FunctionCall`](#function-call) evaluating to a [`ValidationResult`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#catalog_definition.json/$defs/ValidationResult) object `{valid, code, message, severity}` or a boolean) with an optional fallback `message`; in v0.9.1, `condition` is a `DynamicBoolean` and `message` is required. Checks that fail with `"error"` severity (the default, and what a `false` boolean coerces to) mark the component invalid and disable controls such as `Button`, while `"warning"` and `"info"` results display non-blocking feedback.

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [Component Validation & Check Rules](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#component-validation--check-rules) in the protocol specification.

### ChildList

The schema type ([`common_types.json#/$defs/ChildList`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/ChildList) in v1.0; [`common_types.json#/$defs/ChildList`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/ChildList) in v0.9.1) used by container [components](#component) (such as `Column`, `Row`, and `List`) to hold multiple child components in a [surface](#surface)'s flat component list.

A `ChildList` property accepts one of two forms:

1. A static array of `ComponentId` strings (for example, `["header", "body", "footer"]`).
2. A collection template object `{"path": "/items", "componentId": "itemCard"}` that instantiates `componentId` once for each element of the array at `path` in the [data model](#data-model), establishing a collection scope for relative [`@path`](#path) bindings and [`@index`](#index) calls. Template objects use the plain property name `"path"` (not `"@path"`) in both v1.0 and v0.9.1.

See [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/#displaying-dynamic-lists-of-data) and [Collection scopes (relative paths)](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#collection-scopes-relative-paths) in the protocol specification.

### Component

<span id="genui-component"></span>

A declarative UI element defined in a [catalog](#catalog) (such as `Card`, `Button`, `TextField`, or a domain-specific `FlightStatusCard`) and rendered as a native widget by a client [framework adapter](#framework-adapter).

Within a [surface](#surface), component instances are sent in `createSurface` or `updateComponents` as a flat adjacency list rather than a nested tree: each entry has a unique `id` (following Unicode UAX #31 identifier rules in v1.0), a `component` type name, optional `catalogId`, `accessibility` attributes, and `metadata.extensions`, and references children by ID (`ComponentId` or [`ChildList`](#childlist)). Every rendered surface requires one component with `"id": "root"`, which mounts inside the reserved immutable `Surface` container ([`common_types.json#/$defs/Surface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Surface)).

See [Catalogs](/concepts/catalogs/) and [Component model](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#component-model) in the protocol specification.

### Core SDK

<span id="core-library"></span>
<span id="recommended-code-organization"></span>

The UI-framework-agnostic foundational library in each language, shared by both [Agent SDKs](#agent-sdk) and client [framework adapters](#framework-adapter).

The Core SDK implements protocol message models, `Catalog` schemas, reactive surface and [data model](#data-model) state containers (`SurfaceGroupModel`, `SurfaceModel`, `ComponentModel`, and `DataModel`, named `SurfaceViewModel` in Swift and `A2uiCoreSurfaceGroupModel`, `A2uiCoreSurfaceModel`, `A2uiCoreComponentRegistry`, and `A2uiCoreDataModel` in Kotlin, with `A2uiComponentModel` in `compose-runtime`), JSON Pointer resolution, [`@path`](#path) and [`@call`](#call) expression evaluation, [`MessageProcessor`](#messageprocessor), and payload validation.

See [Core SDK](/concepts/sdks/#core-sdk) for official package names across languages.

## D

### Data binding

<span id="data-reference"></span>

Connecting a [component](#component)'s dynamic property (`DynamicString`, `DynamicNumber`, `DynamicBoolean`, `DynamicStringList`, or `DynamicValue` in [`common_types.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json)) to a path in the surface's [data model](#data-model) via a [`DataBinding`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DataBinding) object (`{"@path": "..."}` in v1.0, or `{"path": "..."}` in v0.9.1) instead of a literal value.

Display components (such as `Text`) use one-way reactive bindings that update whenever the bound path changes. Input components (such as `TextField`, `CheckBox`, and `Slider`) establish local two-way bindings that read the current value at the bound path and write user edits back to the local data model immediately without per-keystroke network traffic.

See [`@path`](#path), [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/), and [Data model representation: binding, scope](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#data-model-representation-binding-scope) in the protocol specification.

### Data model

An isolated, reactive JSON state object maintained per [surface](#surface) on the [renderer](#renderer) and shared with the [agent](#agent) that owns the surface.

The agent populates or mutates the data model inline in `createSurface` (v1.0) or incrementally via [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) using [RFC 6901 JSON Pointers](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901). Local user edits remain on the renderer until sent back to the agent selectively in [`Event`](#event) `context` bindings, as resolved arguments to agent-routed function calls ([`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) in v1.0), or in full via transport metadata (`a2uiRendererDataModel` matching [`renderer_data_model.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_data_model.json) in v1.0; `a2uiClientDataModel` matching [`client_data_model.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_data_model.json) in v0.9.1) when `createSurface` sets `"sendDataModel": true`.

See [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/) and [Data model updates: synchronization and convergence](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#data-model-updates-synchronization-and-convergence) in the protocol specification.

## E

### Envelope schema

<span id="message-schema"></span>

A top-level JSON Schema that defines the outer wire structure (`"version"` plus a single message type key) for an [A2UI message](#a2ui-message) exchanged between an [agent](#agent) and a [renderer](#renderer), independent of which [catalog](#catalog) defines the UI [components](#component) and [functions](#function):

1. [`agent_to_renderer.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json) ([`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer)) validates v1.0 messages from agent to renderer (`"version": "1.0"`).
2. [`renderer_to_agent.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json) ([`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent)) validates v1.0 messages from renderer to agent (`"version": "1.0"`).
3. [`server_to_client.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json) validates v0.9.1 (and v0.8) messages from server (agent) to client (renderer), renamed to `agent_to_renderer.json` in v1.0.
4. [`client_to_server.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json) validates v0.9.1 (and v0.8) messages from client (renderer) to server (agent), renamed to `renderer_to_agent.json` in v1.0.

Each envelope schema also has companion JSON array (`*_list.json`) and object-wrapped array (`*_list_wrapper.json`) schemas for batched message delivery.

See [Messages](/concepts/messages/) and [Envelope message structure](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#envelope-message-structure) in the protocol specification.

### Event

The agent-bound variant of a component [`Action`](#action) (`action.event` in [`common_types.json#/$defs/Action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Action)) that notifies the [agent](#agent) of user intent, such as clicking a submit button or choosing an item.

An `event` object declares a required `name`, an optional `context` map of literal values or dynamic bindings, and (in v1.0) an optional `userMessage` (`DynamicString`). When triggered by the user (provided no component [`CheckRule`](#checkrule) fails with `"error"` severity), the [renderer](#renderer) resolves every binding in `context` and `userMessage` against the local [data model](#data-model) and emits an [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) message in [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) containing `name`, `surfaceId`, `sourceComponentId`, ISO 8601 `timestamp`, resolved `context`, and (in v1.0) optional `userMessage` and `metadata.extensions`.

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [`action`](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#action) in the protocol specification.

## F

### Framework adapter

<span id="fw-adapter"></span>
<span id="renderer-sdk"></span>

A UI-framework-specific client library (also called a Renderer SDK), built on top of a [Core SDK](#core-sdk), that renders active surface state from [`MessageProcessor`](#messageprocessor) using native widgets in a target framework such as Flutter, React, Lit Web Components, Angular, SwiftUI, or Jetpack Compose.

Framework adapters include a built-in implementation of the [Basic catalog](#basic-catalog), map A2UI `AccessibilityAttributes` (`label`, `description`, `live`, `hidden`) to platform accessibility APIs, and let teams register custom [catalog](#catalog) component views and local [functions](#function) while the adapter handles reactive state updates.

See [Renderer SDK](/concepts/sdks/#renderer-sdk) for official package names and [How to Integrate A2UI into a Client](/guides/client-integration/).

### Function

<span id="renderer-function"></span>
<span id="agent-function"></span>

A named, typed operation declared in a [catalog](#catalog)'s `functions` map ([`catalog_definition.json#/$defs/FunctionDefinition`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#catalog_definition.json/$defs/FunctionDefinition)) with an argument schema (`args`) and `returnType` (`"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`, `"array"`, `"object"`, `"validationResult"`, `"any"`, or `"void"`). Functions execute logic without sending raw code between the [agent](#agent) and [renderer](#renderer).

In v1.0, whether a function call runs locally or on the agent depends on whether the renderer registers a local implementation, while `allowedCallers` (`"rendererOnly"` by default, `"agentOnly"`, or `"rendererOrAgent"`) and `requiresUserActivation` govern which side and gesture context may invoke it:

1. Renderer functions have a local implementation on the renderer and execute with zero network round-trips for tasks such as string and number formatting, input validation, boolean combinators, or user-gesture actions like `openUrl` (`requiresUserActivation: true`, which requires `"rendererOnly"`). Functions declared with `allowedCallers` set to `"agentOnly"` or `"rendererOrAgent"` (without `requiresUserActivation`) can also be invoked remotely by the agent via [`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction); `"agentOnly"` functions still run on the renderer and cannot be bound to component properties or actions.
2. Agent functions (new in v1.0) have no local implementation on the renderer and execute on the agent for server-side tasks such as checking inventory or verifying credentials; when the renderer resolves a [`FunctionCall`](#function-call)'s catalog and finds no local implementation (whether or not the catalog declares the function, and provided the call is not `@`-prefixed, declared `"agentOnly"`, or blocked by `requiresUserActivation`), the renderer dispatches [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) and awaits `agentFunctionResponse`. (In v0.9.1, functions execute only on the renderer.)

An A2UI function is distinct from a language model tool:

| Aspect      | A2UI function                                                                              | LLM tool                                                              |
| :---------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Executor    | [Renderer](#renderer) (renderer functions) or [agent](#agent) (agent functions).           | Model host or agent environment outside the UI.                       |
| Timing      | During UI rendering, on user interaction, or as an explicit remote call over the protocol. | During model generation before or while producing a response.         |
| Purpose     | UI formatting, input validation, client-side effects, or UI-triggered server lookups.      | Model reasoning, web search, database queries, or backend operations. |
| Declaration | Declared in an A2UI [catalog](#catalog) with typed `args`, `returnType`, and caller rules. | Declared in a tool definition passed to the language model.           |

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/) and [Functions in A2UI Content Execution](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#functions-in-a2ui-content-execution) in the protocol specification.

### Function call

An invocation of a catalog or system [function](#function) represented as a [`FunctionCall`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/FunctionCall) object with [`@call`](#call) in v1.0 (`"call"` in v0.9.1), an optional `catalogId` override, and optional `args`.

Function calls occur in four places across the protocol:

1. Dynamic component property bindings (`DynamicString`, `DynamicNumber`, `DynamicBoolean`, `DynamicStringList`, and `DynamicValue`), re-evaluated reactively when bound [data model](#data-model) paths change.
2. Validation rules ([`CheckRule`](#checkrule) `checks[].condition`), returning a `ValidationResult` or boolean to validate inputs and gate controls.
3. Component [`Action`](#action) handlers (`action.functionCall`), triggered by a user gesture.
4. Explicit remote procedure call envelopes ([`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction) and [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) in v1.0).

See [Actions and Functions](/concepts/actions-and-functions/).

## G

### Generative UI patterns

<span id="known-patterns-of-genui"></span>

Common application layouts for presenting agent-generated [surfaces](#surface) (none of which are required by the A2UI protocol):

1. Chat: Generated surfaces appear in chronological order inside a vertically scrollable conversation view alongside text messages.
2. Canvas: A shared workspace where the user and [agent](#agent) iteratively inspect and update one or more persistent surfaces across turns.
3. Dashboard: Generated surfaces are arranged by topic or role rather than time and remain pinned in fixed regions of the screen.
4. Wizard: Generated surfaces appear step by step to gather structured input for a multi-stage task.

See [Overview: How A2UI Works](/concepts/overview/) and [How to Integrate A2UI into a Client](/guides/client-integration/).

## I

### @index

The reserved v1.0 universal system [function](#function) ([`common_types.json#/$defs/IndexSystemFunction`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/IndexSystemFunction)) that returns the 0-based index of the current item when rendering a [`ChildList`](#childlist) collection template, called as `{"@call": "@index"}` or `{"@call": "@index", "args": {"offset": 1}}` (or `${@index(offset: 1)}` inside `formatString`).

In nested collection templates, `@index` resolves to the innermost enclosing template's index; calling `@index` outside a list template fails evaluation (reporting `EXPRESSION_ERROR` on dynamic bindings or `EXECUTION_ERROR` in [`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction)).

See [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/#displaying-dynamic-lists-of-data) and [The `@index` function](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#the-index-function) in the protocol specification.

### Inference format

<span id="phases-of-parsing-of-model-to-agent-responses"></span>

The structured notation in which a language model writes UI blocks inside [A2UI tags](#a2ui-tag) before the [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) compiles them into [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) wire JSON.

Because inference formats are decoupled from the wire protocol, an agent can switch formats on [`A2uiGenerator`](#a2uigenerator) without modifying client renderers. Supported formats include Express (`ExpressFormatFactory`, the default compact positional DSL that cuts output tokens and decode latency), Direct JSON (`DirectJsonFormatFactory`, raw JSON message arrays with incremental stream healing), and experimental Python-only formats (Atom and Elemental).

When reading a model response (`parseResponse` / `parse_response` or streaming `openStream` / `open_stream`), the Agent SDK parser runs three stages:

1. Tag unwrapping (`unwrap`): Scans model output for opening and closing A2UI tags to separate conversational prose from raw UI blocks.
2. Compilation (`compile`): Translates each raw block from format notation into `agent_to_renderer` messages without checking catalogs or `RendererState`.
3. Validation and state tracking: `parseResponse` / `parse_response` and `openStream` / `open_stream` validate compiled messages against the active [catalogs](#catalog) and update `RendererState`.

See [Inference Formats](/concepts/inference-formats/).

## M

### MacroExpander

An asymmetric catalog and message transformer in the Python [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) (`a2ui.transformers.macros`) that lets developers define coarse-grained composite components on the server with the `@macro` decorator and lower them into standard [catalog](#catalog) primitives before wire transmission.

`MacroExpander.transform_to_inference_catalog` augments a base catalog with component schemas synthesized from `@macro` function type annotations and docstrings for model prompting, and `MacroExpander.transform_to_transport` expands macro components emitted by the model into primitive `createSurface` and `updateComponents` subtrees so client [renderers](#renderer) need no custom widget code.

See [Using Macros](/guides/macros/) and [Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk).

### MessageProcessor

The stateful controller class in each language's [Core SDK](#core-sdk) (`A2uiMessageProcessor` in Kotlin) that processes incoming [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) (and v0.9.1 `server_to_client`) message streams.

`MessageProcessor` validates incoming payloads against registered [catalogs](#catalog), mutates reactive surface and [data model](#data-model) state containers (`SurfaceGroupModel`, `SurfaceModel`, `ComponentModel`, and `DataModel`, named `SurfaceViewModel` in Swift and `A2uiCoreSurfaceGroupModel`, `A2uiCoreSurfaceModel`, `A2uiCoreComponentRegistry`, and `A2uiCoreDataModel` in Kotlin, with `A2uiComponentModel` in `compose-runtime`), resolves JSON Pointers and [`@call`](#call) expressions, enforces function caller and user-activation rules, emits outbound [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) messages (`action`, `callAgentFunction`, `rendererFunctionResponse`, and `error`), and builds renderer [capabilities](#capabilities) and `a2uiRendererDataModel` metadata snapshots.

See [Core SDK](/concepts/sdks/#core-sdk) and [How to Integrate A2UI into a Client](/guides/client-integration/).

## N

### NoAI information

Data categorized by an application as inaccessible to AI models and [agents](#agent), such as payment card details, credentials, or regulated personal records.

Which fields count as NoAI information depends on the product and workflow (for example, medical history may be excluded from AI context in a billing app while required in a clinical diagnostic tool). In generative UI interfaces, keeping NoAI inputs outside agent-bound [`Event`](#event) `context` maps, outside arguments to function calls that can route to the agent via [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction), and off `"sendDataModel": true` surfaces (while visually distinguishing AI-connected inputs from private inputs) lets end users see which data can reach a model.

See [Synchronizing state back to the agent](/concepts/data-binding/#synchronizing-state-back-to-the-agent) in Data Model and Data Binding.

## P

### @path

The reserved v1.0 protocol directive key in a [`DataBinding`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DataBinding) object that points to a value in a surface's [data model](#data-model) using an [RFC 6901 JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901), such as `{"@path": "/reservation/guestEmail"}`.

A path starting with `/` resolves from the root of the surface data model, while a path without a leading slash (such as `{"@path": "guestName"}`) resolves relative to the current item in an enclosing [`ChildList`](#childlist) collection template. In v0.9.1, `DataBinding` uses `"path"` without the `@` prefix ([`common_types.json#/$defs/DataBinding`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/DataBinding)). Even in v1.0, `updateDataModel.path` and `ChildList` template `path` use plain `"path"` because they are fixed schema fields rather than dynamic value unions.

See [Data binding](#data-binding), [Data Model and Data Binding](/concepts/data-binding/), and [Path resolution & scope](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#path-resolution--scope) in the protocol specification.

## R

### Renderer

The client-side runtime inside a host application that advertises supported [catalogs](#catalog) via [capabilities](#capabilities), applies [`agent_to_renderer`](#agent_to_renderer) messages through [`MessageProcessor`](#messageprocessor), renders [surfaces](#surface) as native widgets via a [framework adapter](#framework-adapter), maintains per-surface [data models](#data-model), runs local [functions](#function), and sends [`renderer_to_agent`](#renderer_to_agent) messages back to the [agent](#agent).

See [Renderer SDK](/concepts/sdks/#renderer-sdk) and [How to Integrate A2UI into a Client](/guides/client-integration/).

### renderer_to_agent

The v1.0 protocol [envelope schema](#envelope-schema) ([`renderer_to_agent.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json)) for messages sent from a [renderer](#renderer) to an [agent](#agent). In v0.9.1, this envelope schema is named [`client_to_server.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json).

Every v1.0 `renderer_to_agent` message sets `"version": "1.0"` (v0.9.1 uses `"version": "v0.9"` or `"v0.9.1"`) alongside one of four message keys:

1. [`action`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action) dispatches a user-triggered [`Event`](#event) with its resolved `context`.
2. [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction) (new in v1.0) requests remote execution of an agent-side [function](#function).
3. [`rendererFunctionResponse`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/rendererFunctionResponse) (new in v1.0) returns the `value` or `error` for an agent-initiated [`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction) request.
4. [`error`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/error) reports validation errors (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `UNALLOWED_PARENT`, `UNALLOWED_CHILD`) or runtime faults (`EXPRESSION_ERROR`, `EXECUTION_ERROR`, `INTEGRITY_ERROR`, `INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL`), allowing the agent to prompt the model for self-correction.

See [Messages](/concepts/messages/) and [Renderer-to-agent event messages](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#renderer-to-agent-event-messages) in the protocol specification.

## S

### Surface

An isolated, non-nesting UI region created with a globally unique `surfaceId` via [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage), populated with a flat adjacency list of [components](#component) rooted at `"id": "root"`, backed by its own [data model](#data-model), and removed via [`deleteSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/DeleteSurfaceMessage).

Creating a surface implicitly instantiates the reserved immutable `Surface` container ([`common_types.json#/$defs/Surface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Surface)) with `"child": "root"`. Surfaces cannot nest inside one another, though a host application can display multiple surfaces at the same time (such as separate cards in a chat timeline or panels in a dashboard).

See [Overview: How A2UI Works](/concepts/overview/), [Messages](/concepts/messages/), and [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#createsurface) in the protocol specification.

---

# Inference Formats

> How A2UI decouples the wire protocol from model generation with Express, Direct JSON, and custom inference formats.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/inference-formats/

An inference format defines the structured notation that a language model reads in its system prompt and writes in its response before the server compiles that output into standard A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/). Because compilation happens on the server, every client [renderer](/concepts/sdks/#renderer-sdk) receives the same A2UI JSON over the wire regardless of how the model produced it.

In the diagram below, `A2uiRequestProcessor` coordinates three server-side stages. First, `PromptGenerator` turns the negotiated [catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) schemas, `instructions`, and few-shot `examples` into a format-specific prompt snippet. Next, the model writes UI blocks inside sentinel tags (`<a2ui>...</a2ui>` for Express or `<a2ui-json>...</a2ui-json>` for Direct JSON) alongside conversational prose. Finally, `Parser` or `ResponseStream` heals streaming chunks, compiles each block into wire JSON, and validates every message against `RendererState`.

<InferencePipeline />

## Wire protocol vs. generation formats

Standard JSON is well suited as a wire protocol between an agent server and a client renderer: it is self-describing, language-independent, and validated directly by JSON Schema. Asking a language model to emit raw wire JSON token by token, however, carries avoidable costs:

1. Repeated keys (`"id"`, `"component"`, `"@path"`) and hand-written component identifiers make raw wire JSON roughly three times longer than positional constructor calls.
2. Embedding full JSON Schemas in the system prompt consumes roughly twice as many input tokens as compact component signatures.
3. Deeply nested braces, quotes, and manual component IDs increase syntax and reference errors, especially on smaller, faster models.

Inference formats separate what is best for the model to generate from what is best for the renderer to consume. The [Agent SDKs](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) include two built-in formats and allow custom implementations:

| Format      | Sentinel tags                | SDK support                        | How it represents UI                                                                                                    |
| :---------- | :--------------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Express     | `<a2ui>...</a2ui>`           | TypeScript, Python, Dart (default) | Compact positional DSL with nested component calls and `$/path` data assignments, compiled to flat wire JSON.           |
| Direct JSON | `<a2ui-json>...</a2ui-json>` | TypeScript, Python, Dart           | Standard A2UI wire JSON emitted directly by the model, with Markdown fence stripping and incremental string healing.    |
| Custom      | Format-defined               | TypeScript, Python, Dart           | Any domain-specific grammar or model-tailored notation implemented against the SDK's `InferenceFormatFactory` contract. |

Not every A2UI agent uses free-form model generation. Regulated or deterministic workflows can also construct wire messages directly in server code (driven by a classifier, state machine, or [macro](/guides/macros/)) and send the resulting JSON to the renderer without an LLM compilation step.

## Express vs. wire JSON

In Express, the model calls component constructors with positional or keyword arguments, writes [data model](/concepts/data-binding/) values with `$/path = value`, and nests child components inline instead of inventing string IDs by hand.

The example below uses `Card`, `Column`, `Text`, and `Button` from the Basic Catalog; Express derives signatures dynamically for any custom `catalog.json` you register (whitespace and indentation are optional):

```text title="Express block (indented for readability)"
<a2ui>
$/flight/number = "NH 105"
$/flight/gate = "B12"
root = Card(
  Column([
    Text($/flight/number),
    Text($/flight/gate, "caption"),
    Button(Text("Board now"), action=Event("check_in", {flight: $/flight/number}))
  ])
)
</a2ui>
```

When the compiler reads that `<a2ui>` block, it flattens the nested tree and assigns deterministic IDs (`root`, `root_child`, `root_child_children_0`, and so on). In v1.0, initial data assignments fold into `createSurface.dataModel`; in v0.9.1, the compiler emits `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, and `updateDataModel`:

#### v1.0

```json
[
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "createSurface": {
      "surfaceId": "main",
      "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Card",
          "child": "root_child"
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": ["root_child_children_0", "root_child_children_1", "root_child_children_2"]
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_0",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"@path": "/flight/number"}
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_1",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"@path": "/flight/gate"},
          "variant": "caption"
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_2",
          "component": "Button",
          "child": "root_child_children_2_child",
          "action": {
            "event": {
              "name": "check_in",
              "context": {
                "flight": {"@path": "/flight/number"}
              }
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_2_child",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "Board now"
        }
      ],
      "dataModel": {
        "flight": {
          "number": "NH 105",
          "gate": "B12"
        }
      }
    }
  }
]
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
[
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "createSurface": {
      "surfaceId": "main",
      "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "main",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Card",
          "child": "root_child"
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": ["root_child_children_0", "root_child_children_1", "root_child_children_2"]
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_0",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"path": "/flight/number"}
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_1",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {"path": "/flight/gate"},
          "variant": "caption"
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_2",
          "component": "Button",
          "child": "root_child_children_2_child",
          "action": {
            "event": {
              "name": "check_in",
              "context": {
                "flight": {"path": "/flight/number"}
              }
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "root_child_children_2_child",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "Board now"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "main",
      "path": "/",
      "value": {
        "flight": {
          "number": "NH 105",
          "gate": "B12"
        }
      }
    }
  }
]
```

For the full grammar of Express, see the [A2UI Express specification proposal](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/specification/proposals/express/a2ui_express.md). For the wire message schemas that all formats target, see [`createSurface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage), [`updateComponents`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage), and [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) in the Schema Explorer.

## How inference formats stay swappable

<span id="configuring-inference-formats-across-sdks"></span>

Swapping an inference format requires no changes to catalogs, few-shot examples, or client renderers because every format in the [Agent SDK](/concepts/sdks/#agent-sdk) shares three design properties:

1. Catalog-agnostic prompt synthesis: Rather than hardcoding component names, a format's `PromptGenerator` inspects the negotiated `Catalog` schemas at runtime to derive component signatures, function signatures, and dynamic binding rules.
2. Bidirectional translation (`compile` and `decompile`): Alongside compiling model output into wire messages, each format's `Parser` can decompile wire messages back into the format's text notation. Structured few-shot `examples`, fenced `json` message blocks inside a catalog's `instructions`, and prior conversation turns can therefore be authored once as wire messages and rendered automatically in whichever format is active.
3. Incremental stream compilation and validation: Both one-shot parsing (`parseResponse` / `parse_response`) and chunked streaming (`openStream` / `open_stream`) separate conversational text from UI sentinel blocks, heal in-progress string literals on configured `progressiveKeys` (such as `"text"`), emit incremental wire deltas as statements arrive, and validate every message against `RendererState` so malformed output can be returned to the model for self-correction.

In the Agent SDKs (available for TypeScript, Python, and Dart; the Swift and Kotlin packages focus on client-side rendering), `A2uiGenerator` defaults to `ExpressFormatFactory` and accepts any `InferenceFormatFactory` globally or per request while keeping prompt generation and response parsing identical:

#### TypeScript

```typescript
import {
  A2uiGenerator,
  CatalogConfig,
  DirectJsonFormatFactory,
  ExpressFormatFactory,
} from '@a2ui/agent';

// Uses ExpressFormatFactory by default; pass any InferenceFormatFactory to change it.
const generator = new A2uiGenerator(
  [new CatalogConfig(catalog)],
  undefined,
  new ExpressFormatFactory(),
);

// Prompt synthesis and parsing stay the same regardless of format,
// and an individual request can override the format factory if needed.
const processor = generator.createProcessor(rendererCapabilities, new DirectJsonFormatFactory());
const systemPrompt = processor.promptSnippet;
const parts = processor.parseResponse(llmOutput);
```

#### Python

```python
from a2ui.inference_formats import DirectJsonFormatFactory, ExpressFormatFactory
from a2ui.processor import A2uiGenerator, CatalogConfig

# Uses ExpressFormatFactory by default; pass any InferenceFormatFactory to change it.
generator = A2uiGenerator(
    catalogs=[CatalogConfig(catalog=catalog)],
    inference_format_factory=ExpressFormatFactory(),
)

# Prompt synthesis and parsing stay the same regardless of format,
# and an individual request can override the format factory if needed.
processor = generator.create_processor(
    renderer_capabilities,
    inference_format_factory=DirectJsonFormatFactory(),
)
system_prompt = processor.prompt_snippet
parts = processor.parse_response(llm_output)
```

#### Dart

```dart
import 'package:a2ui_agent/a2ui_agent.dart';

void illustrateFormats(
  Catalog catalog,
  A2uiRendererCapabilities rendererCapabilities,
  String llmOutput,
) {
  // Uses ExpressFormatFactory by default; pass any InferenceFormatFactory to change it.
  final generator = A2uiGenerator(
    catalogs: [CatalogConfig(catalog)],
    inferenceFormatFactory: const ExpressFormatFactory(),
  );

  // Prompt synthesis and parsing stay the same regardless of format,
  // and an individual request can override the format factory if needed.
  final processor = generator.createProcessor(
    rendererCapabilities,
    inferenceFormatFactory: const DirectJsonFormatFactory(),
  );
  final systemPrompt = processor.promptSnippet;
  final parts = processor.parseResponse(llmOutput);
}
```

Express covers v0.9, v0.9.1, and v1.0 generation with lower token cost, while Direct JSON remains useful when serving legacy v0.8 payloads in Python, debugging raw wire payloads, or calling a model fine-tuned directly on A2UI JSON schemas. Teams experimenting with alternative grammars (such as HTML-inspired or S-expression notations; see [`python/a2ui_agent/src/a2ui/inference_formats/experimental/`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_agent/src/a2ui/inference_formats/experimental)) implement the same `InferenceFormatFactory`, `PromptGenerator`, and `Parser` interfaces.

## Token and latency benchmarks

The A2UI evaluation suite (`eval/`) benchmarks each format on the 54-sample `core_v1_0` suite using `gemini-3.8-flash` (`temperature=0.0`). For earlier benchmark background, see [Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats](https://developers.googleblog.com/fast-reliable-a2ui/). Whether thinking is disabled (`thinking_budget=0`) or left unbounded (default), Express reduces both prompt tokens and generated code tokens while matching Direct JSON on accuracy:

| Format and thinking mode           | Median input tokens | Median code tokens | Median thinking tokens | Median total output (`code + thinking`) | Pass@1 / Pass@2       | Judge quality |
| :--------------------------------- | :------------------ | :----------------- | :--------------------- | :-------------------------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------ |
| Direct JSON (`thinking_budget=0`)  | 10,980              | 807                | 0                      | 811                                     | 98.1% / 98.1% (53/54) | 97.2%         |
| Express (`thinking_budget=0`)      | 6,000 (-45.4%)      | 297 (-63.2%, 2.7x) | 0                      | 299 (-63.1%)                            | 98.1% / 98.1% (53/54) | 97.2%         |
| Direct JSON (`unbounded` thinking) | 10,980              | 794                | 1,413                  | 2,320                                   | 98.1% / 98.1% (53/54) | 98.1%         |
| Express (`unbounded` thinking)     | 6,000 (-45.4%)      | 260 (-67.3%, 3.1x) | 1,447                  | 1,789 (-22.9%)                          | 98.1% / 98.1% (53/54) | 98.1%         |

---

# Messages

> Asynchronous bidirectional JSON message types and transport metadata in A2UI.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/messages/

A2UI agents and client renderers communicate by exchanging asynchronous JSON messages in both directions to manage UI surfaces and handle user interactions. These message types can be sent over a variety of transports, including [Agent-to-Agent (A2A)](https://a2a-protocol.org) and [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).

Alongside explicit A2UI messages, implementations can use [metadata](#metadata) to include renderer context in requests sent for other purposes. For example, when a user sends a text prompt, the renderer can attach its supported catalogs or synchronized surface state to the outgoing request.

---

## Agent-to-renderer messages

Agent-to-renderer messages construct surfaces, update component hierarchies and reactive data models, clean up surfaces, invoke client-side functions, and return results for agent-side function calls. Each wire message in either direction is a JSON object with a `"version"` field (`"1.0"` in v1.0, or `"v0.9"` / `"v0.9.1"` in v0.9.1) and a single message key.

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json',
      title: 'v1.0 Agent-to-Renderer Message Schema',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'server_to_client.json',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json',
      title: 'v0.9.1 Server-to-Client Message Schema',
    },
  ]}
/>

### createSurface

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#CreateSurfaceMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'server_to_client.json#CreateSurfaceMessage',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/CreateSurfaceMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `createSurface` message allocates a new UI surface identified by `surfaceId`. The `surfaceId` must be globally unique within the rendering context (the `MessageProcessor` instance on the renderer), which is typically a conversation. Creating a surface implicitly instantiates the reserved [`Surface`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Surface) container component with `child: "root"`. In v1.0, `createSurface` can also include optional surface-level custom extensions under `metadata.extensions` ([`Extensions`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Extensions)).

#### Properties

| Property        | Type    | Required                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| :-------------- | :------ | :---------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surfaceId`     | string  | Yes                           | Unique identifier for the surface.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `catalogId`     | string  | Optional (v1.0), Yes (v0.9.1) | Default catalog identifier for this surface (for example, `travel:flights`). In v1.0, individual components and function calls can specify their own `catalogId` when omitted here.              |
| `sendDataModel` | boolean | Optional                      | When `true`, the renderer attaches the full surface data model in transport metadata (`a2uiRendererDataModel` in v1.0 / `a2uiClientDataModel` in v0.9.1) on every message to the creating agent. |
| `components`    | array   | Optional (v1.0)               | Initial flat list of component definitions, allowing single-message surface creation.                                                                                                            |
| `dataModel`     | object  | Optional (v1.0)               | Initial root data model JSON object for the surface.                                                                                                                                             |
| `metadata`      | object  | Optional (v1.0)               | Surface-level extensions container with optional `extensions` ([`Extensions`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Extensions)).                                            |

> **Note**
  In v1.0, `catalogId` is optional, `components` and `dataModel` can be passed inline to initialize
  a surface in a single message, and the v0.9.1 `theme` property is removed in favor of host
  application styling.

#### Example

Creating a `"flight_search"` surface:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
    "sendDataModel": false,
    "components": [
      {
        "id": "root",
        "component": "Column",
        "children": ["title", "flight_card"]
      },
      {
        "id": "title",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": "Available Flights"
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_card",
        "component": "Card",
        "child": "flight_info"
      },
      {
        "id": "flight_info",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": {"@path": "/flights/0/summary"}
      }
    ],
    "dataModel": {
      "flights": [
        {"summary": "LH458 · BER -> SFO · $680", "price": 680}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "createSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
    "sendDataModel": false
  }
}
```

---

### updateComponents

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#UpdateComponentsMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'server_to_client.json#UpdateComponentsMessage',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/UpdateComponentsMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `updateComponents` message adds or replaces component definitions in an existing surface. Relationships between components are expressed by ID references in a flat adjacency list rather than nested JSON trees, and one component in the surface must have `id: "root"`. In v1.0, individual component definitions in `components` can also carry optional component-level extensions via `metadata.extensions` ([`ComponentCommon`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/ComponentCommon)).

#### Properties

| Property     | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                   |
| :----------- | :----- | :------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surfaceId`  | string | Yes      | Identifier of the surface to update.                                                                                          |
| `components` | array  | Yes      | Non-empty flat array of component objects. Components whose `id` already exists in the surface replace the stored definition. |

#### Example

Populating a surface with a `Column`, header `Text`, and interactive `Button`:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateComponents": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "components": [
      {
        "id": "root",
        "component": "Column",
        "children": ["header", "btn_select_lh458"]
      },
      {
        "id": "header",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": "Outbound Flights"
      },
      {
        "id": "btn_select_label",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": "Select LH458 ($680)"
      },
      {
        "id": "btn_select_lh458",
        "component": "Button",
        "child": "btn_select_label",
        "variant": "primary",
        "action": {
          "event": {
            "name": "select_flight",
            "userMessage": "Selected flight LH458",
            "context": {
              "flightId": "LH458",
              "price": {"@path": "/flights/0/price"}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateComponents": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "components": [
      {
        "id": "root",
        "component": "Column",
        "children": ["header", "btn_select_lh458"]
      },
      {
        "id": "header",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": "Outbound Flights"
      },
      {
        "id": "btn_select_label",
        "component": "Text",
        "text": "Select LH458 ($680)"
      },
      {
        "id": "btn_select_lh458",
        "component": "Button",
        "child": "btn_select_label",
        "variant": "primary",
        "action": {
          "event": {
            "name": "select_flight",
            "context": {
              "flightId": "LH458",
              "price": {"path": "/flights/0/price"}
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

---

### updateDataModel

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#UpdateDataModelMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'server_to_client.json#UpdateDataModelMessage',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `updateDataModel` message updates the surface data model at a targeted location using an [RFC 6901 JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901), allowing the agent to refresh bound values without resending component definitions.

#### Properties

| Property    | Type   | Required                      | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
| :---------- | :----- | :---------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surfaceId` | string | Yes                           | Identifier of the target surface.                                                                                                                                       |
| `path`      | string | Optional                      | RFC 6901 JSON Pointer indicating where to apply the update (for example, `"/selectedFlight"`). When omitted or set to `"/"`, the update replaces the entire data model. |
| `value`     | any    | Yes (v1.0), Optional (v0.9.1) | Value to store at `path`.                                                                                                                                               |

> **Note**
  In **v1.0**, `value` is required; set `"value": null` to delete the key at `path`. In **v0.9.1**,
  `value` is optional, and omitting `value` removes the key at `path`.

#### Examples

#### v1.0

Updating `/selectedFlight`:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "path": "/selectedFlight",
    "value": {
      "flightId": "LH458",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "passengers": 2
    }
  }
}
```

Deleting `/selectedFlight` in v1.0 by setting `"value": null`:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "path": "/selectedFlight",
    "value": null
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

Updating `/selectedFlight`:

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "path": "/selectedFlight",
    "value": {
      "flightId": "LH458",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "passengers": 2
    }
  }
}
```

Deleting `/selectedFlight` in v0.9.1 by omitting `value`:

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "updateDataModel": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "path": "/selectedFlight"
  }
}
```

---

### deleteSurface

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#DeleteSurfaceMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/DeleteSurfaceMessage',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'server_to_client.json#DeleteSurfaceMessage',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_to_client.json/$defs/DeleteSurfaceMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `deleteSurface` message instructs the renderer to unmount the surface identified by `surfaceId` and release its component tree and data model state.

#### Properties

| Property    | Type   | Required | Description                        |
| :---------- | :----- | :------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `surfaceId` | string | Yes      | Identifier of the surface to drop. |

#### Example

Deleting the `"flight_search"` surface:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "deleteSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search"
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "deleteSurface": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search"
  }
}
```
