### callRendererFunction (v1.0 only)

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#CallRendererFunctionMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/CallRendererFunctionMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `callRendererFunction` message is an agent-initiated remote procedure call (RPC) that directs the renderer to execute a catalog function registered on the client (for example, reading device timezone or screen dimensions). Only catalog functions declaring `allowedCallers` as `"agentOnly"` or `"rendererOrAgent"` may be called by the agent.

> **Note**
  `callRendererFunction` is introduced in protocol v1.0. In v0.9.1, `server_to_client.json` does not
  define an agent-to-renderer function invocation message.

#### Properties

| Property         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| :--------------- | :----- | :------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `functionCallId` | string | Yes      | Unique correlation identifier for this call, copied verbatim into [`rendererFunctionResponse`](#rendererfunctionresponse-v10-only).                               |
| `callFunction`   | object | Yes      | [`FunctionCall`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/FunctionCall) object with required `@call`, required `catalogId`, and optional `args`. |
| `surfaceId`      | string | Optional | Surface ID whose data model provides the evaluation context. When omitted, the function executes in an isolated root context with `{}`.                           |

#### Example

Calling a client-side `getDeviceTimezone` function on the renderer:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "callRendererFunction": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "functionCallId": "call_tz_101",
    "callFunction": {
      "@call": "getDeviceTimezone",
      "catalogId": "device:sensors",
      "args": {}
    }
  }
}
```

---

### agentFunctionResponse (v1.0 only)

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'agent_to_renderer.json#AgentFunctionResponseMessage',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/AgentFunctionResponseMessage',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `agentFunctionResponse` message returns the execution result or structured error for a preceding [`callAgentFunction`](#callagentfunction-v10-only) message sent by the renderer.

#### Properties

| Property         | Type   | Required    | Description                                                                                                                        |
| :--------------- | :----- | :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `functionCallId` | string | Yes         | Correlation identifier matching the initiating `callAgentFunction` message.                                                        |
| `value`          | any    | Conditional | Return value produced on success. Exactly one of `value` or `error` must be present.                                               |
| `error`          | object | Conditional | Error object with required `code` (`string`) and `message` (`string`) fields if execution failed. Mutually exclusive with `value`. |

#### Example

Returning baggage allowance data for an agent function call:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "agentFunctionResponse": {
    "functionCallId": "call_baggage_202",
    "value": {
      "allowedBags": 2,
      "maxWeightKg": 23,
      "feePerExtraBag": 75
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Renderer-to-agent messages

Renderer-to-agent messages report user interactions, invoke remote functions on the agent, and return results from agent-initiated client function calls.

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_to_agent.json',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json',
      title: 'v1.0 Renderer-to-Agent Event Schema',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'client_to_server.json',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json',
      title: 'v0.9.1 Client-to-Server Event Schema',
    },
  ]}
/>

### action

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_to_agent.json#action',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/action',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'client_to_server.json#action',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_to_server.json/properties/action',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `action` message notifies the agent that the user triggered an event action on an interactive component (such as clicking a `Button` configured with `action.event`). Before dispatching the message, the renderer resolves any data bindings inside `action.event.context` and `action.event.userMessage` against the local data model. In v1.0, `action` can also include optional renderer-side custom extensions under `metadata.extensions` ([`Extensions`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Extensions)).

#### Properties

| Property            | Type   | Required        | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| :------------------ | :----- | :-------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`              | string | Yes             | Event name declared on the component's `action.event.name`.                                                                                          |
| `surfaceId`         | string | Yes             | Surface ID where the interaction originated.                                                                                                         |
| `sourceComponentId` | string | Yes             | Component `id` that triggered the action.                                                                                                            |
| `timestamp`         | string | Yes             | ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the event occurred.                                                                                        |
| `context`           | object | Yes             | Resolved key-value dictionary from `action.event.context` with all data bindings evaluated to current values.                                        |
| `userMessage`       | string | Optional (v1.0) | Human-readable string resolved from `action.event.userMessage`, suitable for adding to LLM conversation history.                                     |
| `metadata`          | object | Optional (v1.0) | Action-level extensions container with optional `extensions` ([`Extensions`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/Extensions)). |

#### Example

Reporting a `"select_flight"` button action with resolved context:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "action": {
    "name": "select_flight",
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "sourceComponentId": "btn_select_lh458",
    "timestamp": "2026-11-02T10:15:30.000Z",
    "userMessage": "Selected flight LH458",
    "context": {
      "flightId": "LH458",
      "price": 680
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "version": "v0.9",
  "action": {
    "name": "select_flight",
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "sourceComponentId": "btn_select_lh458",
    "timestamp": "2026-11-02T10:15:30.000Z",
    "context": {
      "flightId": "LH458",
      "price": 680
    }
  }
}
```

---

### callAgentFunction (v1.0 only)

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_to_agent.json#callAgentFunction',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/callAgentFunction',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `callAgentFunction` message is a renderer-initiated RPC requesting that the agent execute a function remotely (for example, checking live baggage rules or verifying a backend identifier).

#### Properties

| Property         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| :--------------- | :----- | :------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surfaceId`      | string | Yes      | Surface ID where the call originated.                                                                                                                             |
| `functionCallId` | string | Yes      | Unique correlation identifier for this call, copied verbatim into [`agentFunctionResponse`](#agentfunctionresponse-v10-only).                                     |
| `callFunction`   | object | Yes      | [`FunctionCall`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#common_types.json/$defs/FunctionCall) object with required `@call`, optional `catalogId`, and optional `args`. |

#### Example

Invoking `getBaggageAllowance` on the agent from the renderer:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "callAgentFunction": {
    "surfaceId": "flight_search",
    "functionCallId": "call_baggage_202",
    "callFunction": {
      "@call": "getBaggageAllowance",
      "catalogId": "travel:flights",
      "args": {
        "flightId": "LH458",
        "cabin": "economy"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

### rendererFunctionResponse (v1.0 only)

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_to_agent.json#rendererFunctionResponse',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_to_agent.json/properties/rendererFunctionResponse',
    },
  ]}
/>

The `rendererFunctionResponse` message delivers the renderer's return value or structured execution error for a preceding [`callRendererFunction`](#callrendererfunction-v10-only) message.

#### Properties

| Property         | Type   | Required    | Description                                                                                                                        |
| :--------------- | :----- | :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `functionCallId` | string | Yes         | Correlation identifier matching the initiating `callRendererFunction` message.                                                     |
| `value`          | any    | Conditional | Return value produced on success. Exactly one of `value` or `error` must be present.                                               |
| `error`          | object | Conditional | Error object with required `code` (`string`) and `message` (`string`) fields if execution failed. Mutually exclusive with `value`. |

#### Example

Returning the device timezone for a preceding `callRendererFunction` call:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "rendererFunctionResponse": {
    "functionCallId": "call_tz_101",
    "value": {
      "timeZone": "Europe/Berlin",
      "utcOffsetMinutes": 60
    }
  }
}
```

---

### Metadata

<SchemaChips
  items={[
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_capabilities.json',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_capabilities.json',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'client_capabilities.json',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_capabilities.json',
    },
    {
      version: 'v1.0',
      label: 'renderer_data_model.json',
      href: '/specification/v1.0/schemas/#renderer_data_model.json',
    },
    {
      version: 'v0.9.1',
      label: 'client_data_model.json',
      href: '/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#client_data_model.json',
    },
  ]}
/>

Transport metadata lets the renderer attach A2UI context to outgoing requests sent for other purposes (such as user text prompts in A2A or request metadata in MCP), flowing from the renderer to the agent.

| Metadata key (v1.0)        | Metadata key (v0.9.1)    | Purpose                                                                                       |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `a2uiRendererCapabilities` | `a2uiClientCapabilities` | Advertises supported protocol versions, `supportedCatalogIds`, and optional `inlineCatalogs`. |
| `a2uiRendererDataModel`    | `a2uiClientDataModel`    | Sends full local data models for active surfaces created with `sendDataModel: true`.          |

Renderer capabilities (`a2uiRendererCapabilities` in v1.0 / `a2uiClientCapabilities` in v0.9.1) are an optional mechanism that loosely coupled systems can use to negotiate which protocol versions and catalogs can be used when they are not known in advance. Systems where the agent and client are owned by the same party may not need capability negotiation if the protocol version and catalogs are agreed in advance. Agents can also advertise their static catalog support ahead of time via [`agent_capabilities.json`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_capabilities.json) (v1.0) or [`server_capabilities.json`](/specification/v0.9.1/schemas/#server_capabilities.json) (v0.9.1), such as in an A2A Agent Card.

When any active surface was created with `sendDataModel: true`, the renderer attaches `a2uiRendererDataModel` (or `a2uiClientDataModel` in v0.9.1) on outgoing messages to that agent so local input state stays synchronized without embedding full data models inside `action` payloads.

#### Example

Attaching capabilities and synchronized surface state to an outgoing transport request:

#### v1.0

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "a2uiRendererCapabilities": {
      "1.0": {
        "supportedCatalogIds": [
          "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
          "travel:flights"
        ]
      }
    },
    "a2uiRendererDataModel": {
      "version": "1.0",
      "surfaces": {
        "flight_search": {
          "selectedFlight": "LH458",
          "passengers": 2
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "a2uiClientCapabilities": {
      "v0.9": {
        "supportedCatalogIds": [
          "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json",
          "travel:flights"
        ]
      }
    },
    "a2uiClientDataModel": {
      "version": "v0.9",
      "surfaces": {
        "flight_search": {
          "selectedFlight": "LH458",
          "passengers": 2
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

# SDKs

> Official A2UI Core, Agent, and Renderer SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Dart, Swift, and Kotlin.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/

Official A2UI SDKs are organized into three layers:

- **Core SDK** for shared protocol models and surface state.
- **Agent SDK** for catalog-driven prompt generation and model output compilation.
- **Renderer SDK** for mounting surface state in a client UI framework.

Both the Agent SDK and the Renderer SDK build on their language's Core SDK, so server-side validation and client-side message resolution share one implementation per language. Client-server applications typically pair two layers on each side of a network boundary, such as a Python agent server communicating with a SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose client. Codebases that handle both model inference and UI rendering in the same language, such as TypeScript web apps or Dart and Flutter apps, can use all three layers together in one project.

## Core SDK

Every Agent SDK and Renderer SDK depends on its language's Core SDK, which implements the protocol data structures, reactive state containers, and expression evaluators common to agents and clients.

### Primary functions

1. Parses and serializes A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v1.0, v0.9.1, and v0.8 in TypeScript and Python).
2. Loads [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) JSON Schemas and validates component hierarchies, placement constraints, and message payloads.
3. Maintains per-surface component graphs and JSON [data model](/concepts/data-binding/) state while applying incremental updates by component ID and JSON Pointer path.
4. Evaluates data bindings, collection templates, string interpolation expressions, function invocations, and validation checks.

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                             | Versions                     | Source                                                                                              |
| :--------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/web_core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/web_core)                                                                                                 | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [typescript/core/web_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/core/web_core) |
| Python     | [a2ui-core](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-core/)                                                                                                               | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [python/a2ui_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_core)                 |
| Dart       | [a2ui_core](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_core)                                                                                                                | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [dart/a2ui_core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_core)                     |
| Swift      | [A2UISwiftCore](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift)<br/>[BasicCatalog](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift) | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [swift/core](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/swift/core)                             |
| Kotlin     | [androidx.a2ui](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/a2ui)                                                                                  | v0.9.1                       | [AndroidX a2ui](https://cs.android.com/androidx/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main:a2ui/)  |

All v0.9.1 packages accept v0.9 wire envelopes and catalog IDs. Swift packages are distributed through Swift Package Manager from [`a2ui-project/a2ui`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui) (the `A2UISwiftCore` product exposes the `A2UICore` module), and the AndroidX group on Google Maven publishes the `a2ui-model` and `a2ui-engine` artifacts.

Most applications install a Core SDK automatically through an [Agent SDK](#agent-sdk) or [Renderer SDK](#renderer-sdk), though you can depend on a Core SDK directly to build headless state processors or custom UI adapters. To implement a Core SDK in another language, read [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules) and validate against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core).

## Agent SDK

An Agent SDK connects a language model or agent runtime to the A2UI protocol while leaving model selection, tool execution, and conversation state under your application's control.

### Primary functions

1. Negotiates active [Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/) definitions and protocol versions (v0.9.1 and v1.0) against the capabilities reported by the client renderer (see [Overview](/concepts/overview/)).
2. Generates skills, system prompt instructions, and examples directly from catalog schemas and prompt instructions, replacing hand-written prompts that become outdated when components change.
3. Compiles streaming or batch model output from [inference formats](/concepts/inference-formats/) (such as compact Express syntax, which cuts output tokens without client changes, or chunk-healed Direct JSON) into standard A2UI [wire messages](/concepts/messages/).
4. Validates outgoing messages statefully against active surface state on the server so broken component IDs, placement violations, or schema mismatches can be fed back to the model for self-correction before transmission.
5. Supports optional server-side [`@macro`](/guides/macros/) expansion in Python and integrates with agent frameworks and transports including [Google ADK](https://github.com/google/adk-python) and the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/).

### Packages

| Language   | Published packages                                                                                                                                                           | Versions                     | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| :--------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | [@a2ui/agent](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/agent)                                                                                                                     | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [typescript/agents/a2ui_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/agents/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                       |
| Python     | [a2ui-agent-sdk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-agent-sdk/)<br/>[a2ui-adk](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-adk/) (ADK)<br/>[a2ui-a2a](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-a2a/) (A2A) | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [python/a2ui_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_agent)<br/>[python/a2ui_adk](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_adk)<br/>[python/a2ui_a2a](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/python/a2ui_a2a) |
| Dart       | [a2ui_agent](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                            | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [dart/a2ui_agent](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_agent)                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Swift and Kotlin target client-side rendering; for legacy v0.8 and v0.9 JVM servers, [`kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/kotlin/agent_sdk_legacy) remains in the repository.

### Go and community SDKs

For **Go** services and CLI clients, community-maintained libraries cover server-side validation, streaming parsers, and terminal rendering—including [`satorunooshie/a2ui-go`](https://github.com/satorunooshie/a2ui-go), [`tmc/a2ui`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/tmc/a2ui), [`charmbracelet/a2tea`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/a2tea), and [`muncus/a2term`](https://github.com/muncus/a2term) (listed with version details in [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/)).

To implement a conformance-verified Core or Agent SDK in Go, Rust, C#, or another language, follow the language-agnostic specifications in [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules), verify behavioral parity against the YAML suites in [`conformance/core`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/core) and [`conformance/agent`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance/agent), and open a pull request to add your package to [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/#how-to-submit-a-project).

See [Using a catalog in an agent](/concepts/catalogs/#using-a-catalog-in-an-agent) and [Inference Formats](/concepts/inference-formats/#how-inference-formats-stay-swappable) for TypeScript, Python, and Dart examples of configuring `A2uiGenerator`, negotiating capabilities, and compiling model responses, or run a working agent in the [Quickstart](/quickstart/).

## Renderer SDK

A Renderer SDK connects a Core SDK's resolved surface state to a client UI framework. Official Renderer SDKs include a built-in implementation of the [Basic Catalog](/concepts/catalogs/#the-basic-catalog) styled through the host framework's theming system, and let you register custom catalogs with per-component rendering logic and local functions (see [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/)).

### Primary functions

1. Applies incremental [surface, component, and data model updates](/concepts/messages/) across supported protocol versions (v0.9.1, v1.0, and v0.8 on Web), updating only changed subtrees so unchanged siblings keep focus and local UI state.
2. Evaluates [reactive data bindings](/concepts/data-binding/), nested collection scopes, relative JSON Pointers, and local two-way input edits.
3. Executes [local catalog functions](/concepts/catalogs/#functions) and [reactive validation checks](/specification/v1.0-a2ui/#component-validation--check-rules), enforcing v1.0 caller and user-activation rules.
4. Builds capability and data-model sync metadata payloads for your transport layer, dispatches user action events and structured error messages, and handles v1.0 bidirectional function RPCs.
5. Maps protocol accessibility attributes to host accessibility APIs across Flutter, Web WAI-ARIA, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose.

### Packages

| Framework       | Published packages                                                                                                                                                                            | Versions                     | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Flutter         | [a2ui_flutter](https://pub.dev/packages/a2ui_flutter)                                                                                                                                         | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [dart/a2ui_flutter](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/dart/a2ui_flutter)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| React           | [@a2ui/react](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/react)                                                                                                                                      | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [typescript/renderers/react](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/renderers/react)                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Lit             | [@a2ui/lit](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/lit)                                                                                                                                          | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [typescript/renderers/lit](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/renderers/lit)                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Angular         | [@a2ui/angular](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/angular)                                                                                                                                  | v0.8,&nbsp;v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0 | [typescript/renderers/angular](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/renderers/angular)                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| SwiftUI         | [A2UISwiftUI](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift)<br/>[BasicCatalogSwiftUI](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/Package.swift)                           | v0.9.1,&nbsp;v1.0            | [swift/swiftui](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/swift/swiftui)                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Jetpack Compose | [androidx.a2ui.compose](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/a2ui-compose)<br/>[material3-a2ui](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3) | v0.9.1                       | [AndroidX a2ui](https://cs.android.com/androidx/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main:a2ui/) · [material3-a2ui](https://cs.android.com/androidx/platform/frameworks/support/+/androidx-main:compose/material3/material3-a2ui/) · [Docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/agentic) |

On Web, [`@a2ui/web_core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/web_core) provides the shared Basic Catalog implementation used by React, Lit, and Angular, [`@a2ui/markdown-it`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/markdown-it) ([source](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/typescript/renderers/markdown-it)) renders Markdown inside text components, and [`@a2ui/catalog-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@a2ui/catalog-mcp) adds MCP app components (see [Call MCP Tools from A2UI](/guides/mcp-catalog/)).

See [Registering a catalog in a renderer](/concepts/catalogs/#registering-a-catalog-in-a-renderer) and [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/) for Flutter, Web, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose examples of setting up a message processor, registering component widgets and local functions, and mounting surfaces, or run a React or Flutter client in the [Quickstart](/quickstart/). Read [Authoring Universal Web Components](/guides/authoring-universal-components/) to share custom components across React, Lit, and Angular, or see the [Android Jetpack Compose guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/agentic) for Android integration. Browse [Community Projects](/ecosystem/renderers/) for community renderers, or consult [`blueprints/modules`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/blueprints/modules) and [`conformance`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/conformance) to build a custom framework adapter.

# Render A2UI Inside an MCP App

> Bundle an A2UI renderer inside an MCP App ui:// resource so existing MCP hosts can display interactive A2UI surfaces without native host code.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/guides/a2ui-in-mcp-apps/

An **[MCP App](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/apps/overview)** can bundle an embedded A2UI web renderer inside its `ui://` HTML resource (`text/html;profile=mcp-app`) so existing [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) hosts display interactive A2UI surfaces without adding A2UI renderer code to the host application.

Instead of requiring every MCP client (such as Claude Desktop, the MCP Inspector, or an IDE) to install an A2UI SDK, your MCP server ships a self-contained HTML bundle that mounts `<a2ui-surface>` inside the host's isolated iframe. When tools on the server return `application/a2ui+json` payloads, the embedded app feeds those messages into its own [`MessageProcessor`](/concepts/sdks/#core-sdk) and forwards user actions back through the MCP Apps `tools/call` channel.

> **Note**
  See the [MCP Integration Overview](/guides/mcp-overview/) to compare all four MCP patterns. Use this
  pattern when the outer host supports MCP Apps (`ui://` HTML iframes) rather than A2UI natively.
  For the inverse architecture (embedding third-party MCP App widgets inside your own A2UI host),
  see [Embed MCP Apps in A2UI Surfaces](/guides/mcp-apps-in-a2ui/). If both the host and server support
  A2UI natively and you want to serve reusable A2UI layout templates over MCP without an iframe, see
  [Serve A2UI Layouts from an MCP Server](/guides/a2ui-over-mcp/) and [Call MCP Tools from
  A2UI](/guides/mcp-catalog/).

<img
  src={`${baseUrl}/assets/editor.gif`}
  alt="Generative document editor demo showing selected text in an MCP App triggering contextual A2UI controls to revise content"
/>

---

## Quick start: run the community sample

The [`samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/README.md) directory contains a runnable end-to-end sample with a Python MCP server (`server/server.py`), two single-file Angular micro-apps (`ui://editor/app` for a generative document editor and `ui://basic/app` for a counter), and a sample Angular MCP Apps host (`client/`) that runs a double-iframe sandbox on `http://localhost:4200`.

> **Note**
  The community sample currently emits A2UI `v0.8` messages (`surfaceUpdate`, `dataModelUpdate`, and
  `beginRendering`) rendered by `@a2ui/angular` `0.10.x` inside the micro-apps. The implementation
  walkthrough below updates this pattern to `v1.0` and `v0.9.1` wire payloads with `@a2ui/lit` and
  `@a2ui/web_core`.

### Prerequisites

Install these tools before building and running the sample from a clone of the A2UI repository:

1. Python 3.10 or later and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for the Python MCP server (`server/.python-version` targets Python 3.13 when managed by `uv`).
2. Node.js 22.12 or later with Corepack enabled (`corepack enable`) so `yarn` resolves the standalone Yarn workspace under `samples/community/`.
3. A `GOOGLE_API_KEY` from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) so `server/smart_editor_agent.py` can initialize its Gemini client at startup and generate contextual editor controls (if a Gemini call fails at runtime, the editor falls back to preset slider controls).

### Build the sandbox relay and micro-apps

The server serves single-file HTML bundles from `server/apps/public/`, which are git-ignored in a fresh checkout. Install the `samples/community` workspace dependencies, build the host's outer sandbox relay, and build both micro-apps from the repository root:

```bash
cd samples/community
yarn install

# Build the host's outer sandbox relay (client/public/sandbox_iframe/)
yarn workspace a2ui-in-mcpapps-client run build:sandbox

# Build and inline the Editor micro-app (server/apps/public/editor.html)
yarn workspace basic-mcp-app-angular-editor run build:all

# Build and inline the Basic Counter micro-app (server/apps/public/app.html)
yarn workspace basic-mcp-app-angular run build:all
```

When iterating on a single micro-app, you can run `yarn build:all` directly inside `samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/apps/editor` or `samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/apps/src`.

### Start the MCP server and host client

Open two terminals starting from the repository root.

1. In the first terminal, start the Python MCP server over Server-Sent Events (SSE) on `http://127.0.0.1:8000/sse` (pass `--transport stdio` instead when connecting a desktop MCP host over standard input/output):

   ```bash
   cd samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server
   export GOOGLE_API_KEY="your-api-key"  # Required at startup by smart_editor_agent.py
   uv sync
   uv run python server.py --transport sse --port 8000
   ```

2. In the second terminal, start the sample Angular MCP Apps host on `http://localhost:4200`:

   ```bash
   cd samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/client
   yarn start
   ```

### Try both views in the browser

Open `http://localhost:4200` to test how the sandboxed micro-apps render A2UI payloads returned by the MCP server:

1. Keep **Generative Editor App** selected and click **Load Selected App**. The host calls `get_editor_app` and loads `ui://editor/app` (`editor.html`). Select more than 10 characters of text inside any Editor.js paragraph; the app calls `smart_editor_get_controls`, renders generated A2UI controls (`Slider`, `CheckBox`, or `MultipleChoice`) in the right-hand panel, and calls `smart_editor_apply` when you click **Generate Revision** to rewrite the passage and swap in **Accept** and **Reject** A2UI buttons.
2. Switch the selector to **Basic Counter App** and click **Load Selected App**. The host calls `get_basic_app`, mounts `ui://basic/app` (`app.html`), and delivers the initial A2UI counter surface via `ui/notifications/tool-result`. Clicking **Increase counter** inside the rendered A2UI card calls `increase_counter` on the MCP server and updates `/counter` in place.

---

## Architecture and end-to-end flow

In a native A2UI client integration, the outer host application owns `MessageProcessor` and renders A2UI components directly in its DOM. Embedding A2UI inside an MCP App moves the A2UI runtime across the iframe boundary so any standards-compliant [MCP Apps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) host can render A2UI surfaces unchanged:

1. The **MCP server** publishes one or more self-contained HTML bundles under `ui://` URIs (`mimeType: "text/html;profile=mcp-app"`), alongside entry tools and UI callback tools that return `EmbeddedResource` items carrying `application/a2ui+json` messages.
2. The **MCP host application** connects to the MCP server, inspects `_meta.ui.resourceUri` on the invoked tool, fetches the `ui://` HTML via `resources/read`, and mounts an outer sandbox proxy iframe (`sandbox.html`) that injects the HTML into an inner `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"`.
3. The **embedded MCP App** runs inside that opaque-origin `srcdoc` frame. It bundles its own A2UI web renderer (`MessageProcessor`, component catalogs, and `<a2ui-surface>`), renders `application/a2ui+json` payloads alongside any custom web views (such as the Editor.js canvas in `ui://editor/app`), and translates A2UI action events into JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call` requests relayed through the host.

MCP Apps tool descriptors also scope which actor can invoke each tool via `_meta.ui.visibility` (as shown in [`server/server.py`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/server.py)):

1. Entry tools such as `get_editor_app` and `get_basic_app` declare `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and `visibility: ["model"]`, exposing a single launcher tool to the language model.
2. Fine-grained UI interaction tools such as `increase_counter`, `smart_editor_get_controls`, and `smart_editor_apply` declare `visibility: ["app"]`, allowing the sandboxed view to call them via `tools/call` without adding UI callback noise to the model's tool list.

The sequence diagram below traces the full message lifecycle across the MCP server, the outer MCP host application, the sandbox proxy iframe, and the embedded MCP App running the A2UI renderer. During startup, the host lists tools to discover `_meta.ui.resourceUri` and `_meta.ui.visibility`, invokes the entry tool via `tools/call`, fetches the `ui://` HTML document via `resources/read`, and injects it through the sandbox proxy into the isolated `srcdoc` iframe. Once the embedded app completes the `ui/initialize` and `ui/notifications/initialized` handshake, the host forwards the entry tool's result via `ui/notifications/tool-result`, and the app feeds the embedded `application/a2ui+json` messages into `MessageProcessor` to mount the A2UI surface. When the user clicks a button or submits a form on that surface, `MessageProcessor` dispatches an action, the app sends a JSON-RPC `tools/call` request through the proxy to the host, and the server returns a new `application/a2ui+json` payload (such as `updateDataModel`) that updates the rendered surface in place.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Server as MCP Server
  participant Host as MCP Host Application
  participant Proxy as Sandbox Proxy Iframe
  participant App as Embedded MCP App + A2UI Renderer

  Host->>Server: tools/list (discover _meta.ui.resourceUri & visibility)
  Server-->>Host: Tool definitions
  Host->>Server: tools/call (open_counter_app)
  Server-->>Host: CallToolResult (EmbeddedResource application/a2ui+json)
  Host->>Server: resources/read (ui://counter/app)
  Server-->>Host: TextResourceContents (HTML MCP App bundle)
  Host->>Proxy: Load sandbox proxy and send ui/notifications/sandbox-resource-ready
  Proxy->>App: Inject self-contained HTML into srcdoc (allow-scripts)
  App->>Host: ui/initialize (relayed via Proxy)
  Host-->>App: InitializeResult (hostCapabilities, hostContext)
  App->>Host: ui/notifications/initialized
  Host->>App: ui/notifications/tool-result (initial CallToolResult)
  Note over App: Extract application/a2ui+json and run MessageProcessor.processMessages
  Note over App: User clicks Button on a2ui-surface
  App->>Host: tools/call (increase_counter, arguments from action.context)
  Host->>Server: tools/call (increase_counter)
  Server-->>Host: CallToolResult (updateDataModel in application/a2ui+json)
  Host-->>App: CallToolResult response
  Note over App: Apply updateDataModel to MessageProcessor
```

---

## Build an MCP App with an embedded A2UI renderer

The three steps below build a minimal MCP App using `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`, `@a2ui/lit`, `@a2ui/web_core`, and Vite.

### Step 1: Register the ui:// resource and MCP tools

Start by defining the A2UI messages that your server tools return inside `EmbeddedResource` items (`mimeType: "application/a2ui+json"`). The example below uses the Basic Catalog, though A2UI catalogs are domain-specific and your embedded bundle can register any custom catalog (see [How to Define a Catalog](/guides/defining-a-catalog/)).

In `v1.0`, protocol messages set `"version": "1.0"`, expressions use `@path` and `@call`, component IDs follow UAX #31 identifier syntax (such as `main_column`), and `Text` supports Markdown headings. In `v0.9.1`, messages set `"version": "v0.9"`, expressions use `path` and `call` (with `"returnType": "string"` on string-valued function calls), and `Text.variant` includes `"h3"`.

Here is the initial surface payload returned by `open_counter_app`:

#### v1.0

```json
[
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "createSurface": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Card",
          "child": "main_column"
        },
        {
          "id": "main_column",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": ["title_text", "count_text", "increment_button"]
        },
        {
          "id": "title_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "### Live counter"
        },
        {
          "id": "count_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {
            "@call": "formatString",
            "args": {
              "value": "Count: ${/count}"
            }
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "increment_button_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "Increase counter"
        },
        {
          "id": "increment_button",
          "component": "Button",
          "child": "increment_button_text",
          "variant": "primary",
          "action": {
            "event": {
              "name": "increase_counter",
              "context": {
                "step": 1
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "path": "/",
      "value": {
        "count": 0
      }
    }
  }
]
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
[
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "createSurface": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/catalogs/basic/catalog.json"
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateComponents": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "components": [
        {
          "id": "root",
          "component": "Card",
          "child": "main_column"
        },
        {
          "id": "main_column",
          "component": "Column",
          "children": ["title_text", "count_text", "increment_button"]
        },
        {
          "id": "title_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "Live counter",
          "variant": "h3"
        },
        {
          "id": "count_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": {
            "call": "formatString",
            "args": {
              "value": "Count: ${/count}"
            },
            "returnType": "string"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "increment_button_text",
          "component": "Text",
          "text": "Increase counter"
        },
        {
          "id": "increment_button",
          "component": "Button",
          "child": "increment_button_text",
          "variant": "primary",
          "action": {
            "event": {
              "name": "increase_counter",
              "context": {
                "step": 1
              }
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "path": "/",
      "value": {
        "count": 0
      }
    }
  }
]
```

When the embedded app invokes `increase_counter`, the tool returns only an [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) message (`server_to_client.json` in `v0.9.1`) so the existing surface updates `/count` without rebuilding its component tree:

#### v1.0

```json
[
  {
    "version": "1.0",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "path": "/count",
      "value": 1
    }
  }
]
```

#### v0.9.1

```json
[
  {
    "version": "v0.9",
    "updateDataModel": {
      "surfaceId": "counter_card",
      "path": "/count",
      "value": 1
    }
  }
]
```

Register the `ui://counter/app` HTML resource (`text/html;profile=mcp-app`), the model-facing `open_counter_app` entry tool, and the app-only `increase_counter` callback tool on your MCP server:

#### TypeScript

```typescript
import fs from 'node:fs';
import {
  RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
  registerAppResource,
  registerAppTool,
} from '@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/server';
import {McpServer} from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js';
import {z} from 'zod';

const A2UI_MIME_TYPE = 'application/a2ui+json';
const APP_URI = 'ui://counter/app';
let count = 0;

export function createCounterMcpServer(bundlePath: string): McpServer {
  const server = new McpServer({name: 'a2ui-counter-mcp-app', version: '1.0.0'});

  registerAppResource(
    server,
    'Counter MCP App',
    APP_URI,
    {
      description: 'Self-contained MCP App with an embedded A2UI renderer.',
      mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
    },
    async () => ({
      contents: [
        {
          uri: APP_URI,
          mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
          text: fs.readFileSync(bundlePath, 'utf8'),
        },
      ],
    }),
  );

  registerAppTool(
    server,
    'open_counter_app',
    {
      title: 'Open Counter App',
      description: 'Opens the counter view and returns its initial A2UI surface.',
      inputSchema: {},
      _meta: {
        ui: {
          resourceUri: APP_URI,
          visibility: ['model'],
        },
      },
    },
    async () => ({
      content: [
        {type: 'text', text: `Counter opened at ${count}.`},
        {
          type: 'resource',
          resource: {
            uri: 'a2ui://counter-card',
            mimeType: A2UI_MIME_TYPE,
            text: JSON.stringify(buildInitialSurfacePayload(count)),
          },
        },
      ],
    }),
  );

  server.registerTool(
    'increase_counter',
    {
      title: 'Increase Counter',
      description: 'Increments the counter and returns an A2UI updateDataModel payload.',
      inputSchema: {
        step: z.number().int().default(1),
      },
      _meta: {
        ui: {
          visibility: ['app'],
        },
      },
    },
    async ({step}) => {
      count += step;
      const update = [
        {
          version: '1.0',
          updateDataModel: {
            surfaceId: 'counter_card',
            path: '/count',
            value: count,
          },
        },
      ];
      return {
        content: [
          {type: 'text', text: `Count is now ${count}.`},
          {
            type: 'resource',
            resource: {
              uri: 'a2ui://counter-card/data',
              mimeType: A2UI_MIME_TYPE,
              text: JSON.stringify(update),
            },
          },
        ],
      };
    },
  );

  return server;
}
```

#### Python

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from mcp import types
from mcp.server.lowlevel import Server
from mcp.server.lowlevel.helper_types import ReadResourceContents

A2UI_MIME_TYPE = "application/a2ui+json"
MCP_APP_MIME_TYPE = "text/html;profile=mcp-app"
APP_URI = "ui://counter/app"
BUNDLE_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / "dist" / "index.html"

app = Server("a2ui-counter-mcp-app")
count = 0

# Requires mcp<2 (pip install "mcp>=1.20,<2") for the 1.x low-level Server decorators.
@app.list_resources()
async def list_resources() -> list[types.Resource]:
    return [
        types.Resource(
            uri=APP_URI,
            name="Counter MCP App",
            mimeType=MCP_APP_MIME_TYPE,
            description="Self-contained MCP App with an embedded A2UI renderer.",
        )
    ]

@app.read_resource()
async def read_resource(uri: str) -> list[ReadResourceContents]:
    if str(uri) != APP_URI:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown resource: {uri}")
    return [
        ReadResourceContents(
            content=BUNDLE_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
            mime_type=MCP_APP_MIME_TYPE,
        )
    ]

@app.list_tools()
async def list_tools() -> list[types.Tool]:
    return [
        types.Tool(
            name="open_counter_app",
            title="Open Counter App",
            description="Opens the counter view and returns its initial A2UI surface.",
            inputSchema={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
            _meta={"ui": {"resourceUri": APP_URI, "visibility": ["model"]}},
        ),
        types.Tool(
            name="increase_counter",
            title="Increase Counter",
            description="Increments the counter and returns an A2UI updateDataModel payload.",
            inputSchema={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"step": {"type": "integer", "default": 1}},
            },
            _meta={"ui": {"visibility": ["app"]}},
        ),
    ]

@app.call_tool()
async def handle_call_tool(
    name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]
) -> types.CallToolResult:
    global count
    if name == "open_counter_app":
        payload = build_initial_surface_payload(count)
        return types.CallToolResult(
            content=[
                types.TextContent(type="text", text=f"Counter opened at {count}."),
                types.EmbeddedResource(
                    type="resource",
                    resource=types.TextResourceContents(
                        uri="a2ui://counter-card",
                        mimeType=A2UI_MIME_TYPE,
                        text=json.dumps(payload),
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )

    if name == "increase_counter":
        count += int(arguments.get("step", 1))
        update = [
            {
                "version": "1.0",
                "updateDataModel": {
                    "surfaceId": "counter_card",
                    "path": "/count",
                    "value": count,
                },
            }
        ]
        return types.CallToolResult(
            content=[
                types.TextContent(type="text", text=f"Count is now {count}."),
                types.EmbeddedResource(
                    type="resource",
                    resource=types.TextResourceContents(
                        uri="a2ui://counter-card/data",
                        mimeType=A2UI_MIME_TYPE,
                        text=json.dumps(update),
                    ),
                ),
            ]
        )

    raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool: {name}")
```

### Step 2: Embed the A2UI renderer and forward actions in the MCP App

Inside the MCP App project, install `@a2ui/lit`, `@a2ui/markdown-it`, `@a2ui/web_core`, `lit`, and `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`:

```bash
npm install @a2ui/lit @a2ui/markdown-it @a2ui/web_core lit @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps
```

Create an `index.html` entry point with a mount element for your surface:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Counter MCP App</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <main id="surface-root"></main>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

In `src/main.ts`, register `renderMarkdown` via `setMarkdownRenderer`, initialize `MessageProcessor` with `basicCatalog` (or your custom catalog), mount `<a2ui-surface>` when a surface is created, and use `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` to handle the `ui/initialize` handshake, incoming `ui/notifications/tool-result` payloads, automatic iframe resizing (`autoResize: true`), and outbound `tools/call` requests whenever a component dispatches an [action](/concepts/actions-and-functions/):

#### v1.0

```typescript
import {html, render} from 'lit';
import '@a2ui/lit';
import {renderMarkdown} from '@a2ui/markdown-it';
import {
  basicCatalog,
  MessageProcessor,
  setMarkdownRenderer,
  type ProcessableMessagePayload,
} from '@a2ui/web_core/v1_0';
import {App} from '@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps';
import type {CallToolResult} from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js';

setMarkdownRenderer(renderMarkdown);

const A2UI_MIME_TYPE = 'application/a2ui+json';
const rootEl = document.getElementById('surface-root')!;

const app = new App(
  {name: 'counter-mcp-app', version: '1.0.0'},
  {availableDisplayModes: ['inline']},
  {autoResize: true},
);

function applyToolResult(result: CallToolResult): void {
  for (const block of result.content ?? []) {
    if (
      block.type === 'resource' &&
      'text' in block.resource &&
      (block.resource.mimeType === A2UI_MIME_TYPE ||
        block.resource.mimeType === 'application/json+a2ui')
    ) {
      const messages = JSON.parse(block.resource.text) as ProcessableMessagePayload;
      processor.processMessages(messages);
    }
  }
}

const processor = new MessageProcessor([basicCatalog], async action => {
  const result = await app.callServerTool({
    name: action.name,
    arguments: action.context,
  });
  applyToolResult(result);
});

processor.onSurfaceCreated(surface => {
  render(html`<a2ui-surface .surface=${surface}></a2ui-surface>`, rootEl);
});

app.ontoolresult = params => {
  applyToolResult(params);
};

await app.connect();
```

#### v0.9.1

```typescript
import {html, render} from 'lit';
import {basicCatalog} from '@a2ui/lit/v0_9';
import {renderMarkdown} from '@a2ui/markdown-it';
import {
  MessageProcessor,
  setMarkdownRenderer,
  type ProcessableMessagePayload,
} from '@a2ui/web_core/v0_9';
import {App} from '@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps';
import type {CallToolResult} from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js';

setMarkdownRenderer(renderMarkdown);

const A2UI_MIME_TYPE = 'application/a2ui+json';
const rootEl = document.getElementById('surface-root')!;

const app = new App(
  {name: 'counter-mcp-app', version: '1.0.0'},
  {availableDisplayModes: ['inline']},
  {autoResize: true},
);

function applyToolResult(result: CallToolResult): void {
  for (const block of result.content ?? []) {
    if (
      block.type === 'resource' &&
      'text' in block.resource &&
      (block.resource.mimeType === A2UI_MIME_TYPE ||
        block.resource.mimeType === 'application/json+a2ui')
    ) {
      const messages = JSON.parse(block.resource.text) as ProcessableMessagePayload;
      processor.processMessages(messages);
    }
  }
}

const processor = new MessageProcessor([basicCatalog], async action => {
  const result = await app.callServerTool({
    name: action.name,
    arguments: action.context,
  });
  applyToolResult(result);
});

processor.onSurfaceCreated(surface => {
  render(html`<a2ui-surface .surface=${surface}></a2ui-surface>`, rootEl);
});

app.ontoolresult = params => {
  applyToolResult(params);
};

await app.connect();
```

If you need to include full form state from the surface `DataModel` alongside explicit `action.context` entries (as the Editor sample does when submitting slider and checkbox adjustments to `smart_editor_apply`), read `processor.getSurface(action.surfaceId)?.dataModel.get('/')` inside the action callback and merge it into `arguments`. You can also speak the underlying JSON-RPC 2.0 `window.parent.postMessage` protocol directly without `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`; see [`server/apps/src/src/main.ts`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/apps/src/src/main.ts) for a zero-wrapper reference.

### Step 3: Bundle into a single self-contained HTML file

MCP Apps load inside a `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and no base server URL, so external `<script src="...">`, `<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">`, or code-split ES module chunks cannot resolve relative paths. Bundle your renderer and application code into one standalone HTML file before serving it from `resources/read`:

#### Vite (Lit or React)

Install [`vite-plugin-singlefile`](https://github.com/richardtallent/vite-plugin-singlefile) (`npm install -D vite vite-plugin-singlefile`) and enable it in `vite.config.ts` so `vite build` inlines every JavaScript and CSS asset directly into `dist/index.html`:

```typescript
import {defineConfig} from 'vite';
import {viteSingleFile} from 'vite-plugin-singlefile';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [viteSingleFile()],
  build: {
    outDir: 'dist',
    emptyOutDir: true,
  },
});
```

#### Angular CLI + esbuild

Angular production builds emit split ES module chunks and `<link rel="modulepreload">` tags by default. Follow [`samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/apps/inline.js`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-in-mcpapps/server/apps/inline.js): run `ng build`, bundle `main.js` into one ESM file with `esbuild --bundle --format=esm`, inline `<script type="module">` and `<style>` blocks into `index.html`, and strip `<link rel="modulepreload">` tags so the iframe does not issue blocked relative requests.

---

## Advanced considerations

### Sandbox and Content Security Policy constraints

An MCP App runs inside a double-iframe sandbox where the inner `srcdoc` frame carries `sandbox="allow-scripts"` without `allow-same-origin`. Keep three browser constraints in mind when building surfaces for this environment:

1. Because the inner frame runs under an opaque `null` origin (`window.location.origin === "null"`), `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `IndexedDB`, and `document.cookie` throw `SecurityError`. Store transient UI state in the A2UI surface [Data Model](/concepts/data-binding/) and persist durable state on the MCP server through `tools/call`.
2. When writing custom `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` handlers instead of using `App` from `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`, check `event.source === window.parent` before trusting incoming JSON-RPC messages, and pass an explicit target origin to `window.parent.postMessage` whenever the outer host origin is known.
3. MCP App hosts enforce a restrictive Content Security Policy (`connect-src 'none'`, with external media and fonts blocked unless allowlisted). If A2UI components such as `Image`, `Video`, or `AudioPlayer` reference external HTTPS URLs, declare those origins in `_meta.ui.csp` on the HTML content item returned from `resources/read` so the outer sandbox proxy adds them to the frame's CSP header:

```json
{
  "contents": [
    {
      "uri": "ui://counter/app",
      "mimeType": "text/html;profile=mcp-app",
      "text": "<!doctype html><html>...</html>",
      "_meta": {
        "ui": {
          "csp": {
            "resourceDomains": ["https://images.example.com"],
            "connectDomains": []
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Synchronizing light and dark themes with the MCP host

The Basic Catalog stylesheet in `@a2ui/web_core` defines its design tokens (`--a2ui-color-background`, `--a2ui-color-surface`, `--a2ui-color-on-surface`, `--a2ui-color-primary`, and `--a2ui-color-border`) with CSS `light-dark()`, and supports explicit `.a2ui-light` and `.a2ui-dark` root classes.

To match the outer MCP host's active color scheme rather than only the operating system default, apply the theme reported by `app.getHostContext()` on startup and update it whenever `ui/notifications/host-context-changed` fires:

```typescript
function applyHostTheme(theme: string | undefined): void {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  root.classList.toggle('a2ui-dark', theme === 'dark');
  root.classList.toggle('a2ui-light', theme === 'light');
}

// Register before the existing await app.connect() call in src/main.ts:
app.onhostcontextchanged = context => {
  applyHostTheme(context.theme);
};

// After the existing await app.connect() call in src/main.ts resolves:
applyHostTheme(app.getHostContext()?.theme);
```

You can also override `--a2ui-color-primary`, `--a2ui-border-radius`, or `--a2ui-font-family-title` on `:root` in your app's CSS to match your product's typography and accent palette.

### Validating server payloads before returning tool results

Because A2UI JSON messages travel inside MCP `CallToolResult` payloads and are parsed inside the client's sandboxed iframe, an invalid component property or missing child ID fails inside the iframe rather than at the server boundary. Validate generated or static message arrays on your MCP server before returning them from `tools/call` using `validatePayload` (`validate_payload` in Python) from the A2UI Agent SDK.

Swift (`A2UISwiftCore` and `A2UISwiftUI`) and Kotlin (`androidx.a2ui` and `androidx.a2ui.compose`) focus on client-side rendering rather than server-side generation, so Agent SDK payload validation is available in TypeScript, Python, and Dart:

#### TypeScript

```typescript
import {validatePayload} from '@a2ui/agent';
import {basicCatalog} from '@a2ui/web_core/v1_0';

// Throws A2uiValidationError if a v1.0 renderer holding basicCatalog would reject the messages.
validatePayload([basicCatalog], a2uiPayload);
```

#### Python

```python
from a2ui.core.basic_catalog import BasicCatalog
from a2ui.utils import validate_payload

# Raises A2uiValidationError if a v1.0 renderer holding BasicCatalog would reject the messages.
validate_payload([BasicCatalog("1.0")], a2ui_payload)
```

#### Dart

```dart
import 'package:a2ui_agent/a2ui_agent.dart';
import 'package:a2ui_core/a2ui_core.dart';

// Throws A2uiValidationError if a v1.0 renderer holding BasicCatalog.v1_0() would reject the messages.
final parsed = AgentToRendererMessagePayload.fromJson(
  a2uiPayload,
  protocolVersion: A2uiProtocolVersion.v1_0,
);
validatePayload([BasicCatalog.v1_0()], parsed.messages);
```

# Serve A2UI Layouts from an MCP Server

> Serve reusable A2UI layout templates and per-call data updates from a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

Canonical URL: https://a2ui.org/guides/a2ui-over-mcp/

A **[Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)** server can deliver interactive A2UI surfaces by publishing static layout templates as `a2ui://` resources (`application/a2ui+json`) and returning per-call [`updateDataModel`](/specification/v1.0/schemas/#agent_to_renderer.json/$defs/UpdateDataModelMessage) messages from tools.

Instead of repeating the component tree on every tool invocation, the server sends the layout once through `resources/read` and returns only JSON values on `tools/call`. Clients cache the layout by URI and update the surface state whenever a tool runs.

> **Note**
  See the [MCP Integration Overview](/guides/mcp-overview/) to compare all four MCP patterns. To
  configure `@a2ui/catalog-mcp` and invoke MCP tools from Lit, React, or Angular surfaces, see [Call
  MCP Tools from A2UI](/guides/mcp-catalog/). If your MCP server ships a sandboxed HTML widget (`ui://`,
  `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) rather than A2UI JSON messages, see [Embed MCP Apps in A2UI
  Surfaces](/guides/mcp-apps-in-a2ui/).

<video
  width="100%"
  height="auto"
  controls
  playsinline
  style={{
    display: 'block',
    aspectRatio: '16 / 9',
    objectFit: 'cover',
    borderRadius: '8px',
    marginBottom: '24px',
  }}
>
  <source src={`${baseUrl}/assets/guides-a2ui-over-mcp-tour.mp4`} type="video/mp4" />
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

## Quick start: run the recipe sample

The repository includes an end-to-end recipe studio sample ([`samples/community/mcp/a2ui-over-mcp-recipe/`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-over-mcp-recipe/README.md)) with a Python MCP server and a Lit web client. The recipe sample emits A2UI `v0.9` messages; for a client-side A2UI `v1.0` sample built on `basicCatalog` and `mcpCatalog`, see [`samples/community/mcp/a2ui-over-mcp-filesystem/`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/blob/main/samples/community/mcp/a2ui-over-mcp-filesystem/README.md).

### Prerequisites

Install these tools before running the sample from a clone of the A2UI repository:

1. Python 3.10 or later for the MCP server.
2. [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to install Python dependencies and run the server.
3. Node.js 22.12 or later with Corepack enabled (`corepack enable`) for the MCP Inspector and the web client.

### Start the MCP server

Start the recipe MCP server on `http://127.0.0.1:8000/sse` using Server-Sent Events (SSE):

```bash
cd samples/community/mcp/a2ui-over-mcp-recipe
uv run .
```

> **Note**
  The sample points at the local Agent SDK package in the monorepo. In standalone Python projects,
  install `a2ui-agent-sdk` from PyPI (`pip install a2ui-agent-sdk` or `uv add a2ui-agent-sdk`).

### Inspect with the MCP Inspector

In a second terminal, open the [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector) against the running SSE endpoint:

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest --web --transport sse --server-url http://localhost:8000/sse
```

Open `http://localhost:6274` in your browser to inspect the templates and tool outputs directly:

1. Select **List Resources** to view `a2ui://recipe-form` and `a2ui://recipe-card`.
2. Read either resource to inspect the static A2UI template (`createSurface` and `updateComponents`) and its data-binding paths.
3. Select **List Tools** to view `get_recipe_form_a2ui` and `get_recipe_a2ui`, each carrying a `_meta.ui.resourceUri` pointer to its template resource.
4. Run `get_recipe_form_a2ui` to inspect the initial form selection values wrapped in an `updateDataModel` message.
5. Run `get_recipe_a2ui` with `cookingStyle` and `protein` arguments to inspect the generated recipe fields returned as an `updateDataModel` message.

### Run the web client

In a separate terminal starting from the repository root, build the local TypeScript packages used by the sample, install the `samples/community` workspace dependencies, and start Vite:

```bash
yarn install
yarn workspace @a2ui/catalog-mcp run build
yarn workspace @a2ui/lit run build

cd samples/community
yarn install
yarn workspace a2ui-over-mcp-recipe-client run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:5173`. On startup, the client connects to the MCP server over SSE and calls `get_recipe_form_a2ui`. It reads `_meta.ui.resourceUri` to fetch and cache `a2ui://recipe-form`, creates the form surface, and applies the returned `updateDataModel` (`Grilled` and `Chicken`). Selecting new preferences and clicking **Get Recipe** invokes `get_recipe_a2ui`, fetches `a2ui://recipe-card` on first use, and populates the recipe card on the right.

<img
  src={`${baseUrl}/assets/recipe_sample.gif`}
  alt="Recipe Studio sample showing preference pickers on the left and a generated recipe card on the right"
/>

Browse additional MCP integrations in [`samples/community/mcp/`](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui/tree/main/samples/community/mcp).
